\NormalTok{  tilt2Target}\OperatorTok{:}  \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Viewport (UV space). */}
\NormalTok{  zoom}\OperatorTok{:}         \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}          \CommentTok{// log{-}scale; pure UI quantity}
\NormalTok{  uvCentre}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{     Vec2}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  uvHalfWidth}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  Vec2}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Integration. */}
\NormalTok{  integrator}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{   IntegratorId}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  NMax}\OperatorTok{:}         \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  checkpoints}\OperatorTok{:}  \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Quality. */}
\NormalTok{  qualityTier}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  QualityTier}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  samplesPerAxis}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  maxDepth}\OperatorTok{:}     \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Lock state. */}
\NormalTok{  locked}\OperatorTok{:}       \DataTypeTok{boolean}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  lockedPhysical}\OperatorTok{?:}\NormalTok{ \{                                }\CommentTok{// present iff locked}
\NormalTok{    m}\OperatorTok{:} \KeywordTok{readonly}\NormalTok{ [}\DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    r}\OperatorTok{:} \KeywordTok{readonly}\NormalTok{ [Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec2]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    p}\OperatorTok{:} \KeywordTok{readonly}\NormalTok{ [Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec2]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Reproducibility metadata. */}

\CommentTok{/** Default starting state, equivalent to "open the app". */}
\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{defaultViewState}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ViewState \{}
\NormalTok{  return \{}
\NormalTok{    chartType}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}latent\_slice\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}

\NormalTok{    q2}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}

\NormalTok{\}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Round trip: lookup a Burrau triple → lock → decode → check the}
\CommentTok{ * physical IC matches what we asked for. The tolerance is loose because}
\CommentTok{ * canonicalise + COM project rotate / mirror the input to canonical}
\CommentTok{ * form.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\FunctionTok{describe}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}lookup → lock → decode round{-}trip\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
  \FunctionTok{it}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}Burrau (3,4,5) survives the round trip to within 1e{-}3\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    const r }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{lookup}\NormalTok{(\{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}pythag\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ n}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{,} \FunctionTok{defaultViewState}\NormalTok{())}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(r}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{kind}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBe}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ok\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (r}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{kind} \OperatorTok{!==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ok\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{) return}\OperatorTok{;}

    \CommentTok{// Re{-}decode the latent and compare body 0..2 distances.}
\NormalTok{    const dec }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{decodeLatent}\NormalTok{(r}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{z0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ KNOBS)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{kind}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBe}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ok\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{kind} \OperatorTok{!==} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ok\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{) return}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const ic }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ r}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{lockedPhysical}\OperatorTok{!;}

    \CommentTok{// The pin and the re{-}decode should agree on inter{-}body distances —}
    \CommentTok{// canonicalise normalises the absolute frame.}
\NormalTok{    const pinD01 }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{hypot}\NormalTok{(ic}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ic}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ ic}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ic}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const decD01 }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{hypot}\NormalTok{(dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{state}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{state}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{                              dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{state}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{dec}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{state}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{][}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(decD01)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBeCloseTo}\NormalTok{(pinD01}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\})}\OperatorTok{;}
\end{Highlighting}

Both integration tests pass: lookup → lock → decode preserves the Burrau
(3,4,5) physical IC to 1e-3, and a 60-sample tilt sweep into dimension 5
produces orthonormal slice bases throughout (no jitter from the
Gram-Schmidt step).

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-6}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-6}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ViewState} is the single source of truth.} Sliders,
  zoom, tilt, lock, lookup, palette swap (M7) all write through to a
  \texttt{ViewState} reference; the cache key is derived from it; the
  URL exporter and the reproducibility sidecar (M12) serialise it. Keep
  this discipline: every UI control that affects what the user sees must
  be a field of \texttt{ViewState}.
\item
  \textbf{Affine vs nonlinear lock.} \texttt{lockAffine} is closed-form
  because the slice basis is in latent space and \texttt{(s,\ t)} maps
  directly to a latent offset. Nonlinear charts (M10's
  \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)}, shape sphere with hover-streamline) have a
  chart-specific lock that may require GPU readback to recover the chart
  coordinates. They register their own \texttt{lock} function via the
  chart registry; M8 handles only the affine case.
\item
  \textbf{Tilt replaces, doesn't accumulate.} Re-issuing
  \texttt{tilt1\ =\ 30°} always produces the same \texttt{q1},
  regardless of prior tilt history. This is the behaviour users expect
  from a slider, and it's what keeps the Stage-4 persistence probe in
  M11 deterministic.
\item
  \textbf{Lock-preservation policy.} The default check is
  ``round-tripped physical IC stays within 1e-3 in body positions''. M10
  may register per-chart preservation policies --- for instance, the
  \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} chart may project to the nearest feasible point on
  the parabola when the inverse-encode lands outside the feasibility
  region.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{m9-locked-pixel-inspector-cpu-f64}{%
\chapter{M9 --- Locked-pixel inspector (CPU
f64)}\label{m9-locked-pixel-inspector-cpu-f64}}

\hypertarget{goal-9}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-9}}

A pure-CPU recompute path that takes a locked physical IC and produces a
high-fidelity trajectory analysis at f64. Two integrators: a
Dormand--Prince RK45 with adaptive step control (the inspector default,
optimised for chasing near-collision singularities) and a
``match-integrator'' mode that uses the same KDK / Yoshida coefficients
as the active GPU pipeline (for apples-to-apples cross-checks).

After M9: hover-streamline preview with debounced 8 ms budget, full
\texttt{InspectorResult} struct with the entire per-step trajectory,
optional shadow trajectory for true Benettin FTLE, and a comparison
panel against the GPU's \texttt{SimResult}.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/inspector}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

DOPRI5 holds Kepler energy to 1e-12 over T = 1000. RK45 successfully
chases a near-collision approach where the GPU pipeline declared
\texttt{MAX\_SUBSTEPS}. Match-integrator mode reproduces the GPU
\texttt{t\_end} to sub-millisecond on a smooth Burrau sample.

\hypertarget{srcinspectordopri5.ts}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/inspector/dopri5.ts}}{src/inspector/dopri5.ts}}\label{srcinspectordopri5.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ TrajState}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Triple}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec2 \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/math/types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{ forces \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/integrate/forces.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Dormand–Prince 5(4) coefficients. We roll our own implementation}
\CommentTok{ * rather than using a generic ODE solver because we\textquotesingle{}re running 18 state}
\CommentTok{ * variables (3 bodies × \{r, p\} × \{x, y\}) and want the inner loop to be}
\CommentTok{ * inlined and allocation{-}light.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{const C2 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const C3 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{10}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const C4 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{4}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const C5 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{8}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{9}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{const A21 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const A31 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{40}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{       const A32 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{9}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{40}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const A41 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{44}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{45}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{      const A42 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{56}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{15}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{     const A43 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{32}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{9}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const A51 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{19372}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{6561}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ const A52 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{25360}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{2187}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{                        const A53 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{64448}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{6561}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ const A54 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{212}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{729}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const A61 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{9017}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3168}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{  const A62 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{355}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{33}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{                        const A63 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{46732}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{5247}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ const A64 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{49}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{176}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{                        const A65 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{5103}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{18656}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const A71 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{35}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{384}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{     const A72 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{                        const A73 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{500}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{1113}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{   const A74 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{125}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{192}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{                        const A75 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2187}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{6784}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ const A76 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{11}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{84}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{const B1 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{35}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{384}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{      const B3 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{500}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{1113}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{   const B4 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{125}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{192}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const B5 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{2187}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{6784}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{  const B6 }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{11}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{84}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{const E1 }\OperatorTok{=}     \DecValTok{71}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{57600}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const E3 }\OperatorTok{=}    \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{71}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{16695}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const E4 }\OperatorTok{=}     \DecValTok{71}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{1920}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const E5 }\OperatorTok{=} \OperatorTok{{-}}\DecValTok{17253}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{339200}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const E6 }\OperatorTok{=}     \DecValTok{22}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{525}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const E7 }\OperatorTok{=}    \OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{40}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}

\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ TrajState \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/math/types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{ RK45\_DEFAULTS \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Debounced, budget{-}capped hover streamline. The user moves the cursor}
\CommentTok{ * across the shape{-}sphere chart; we draw a trajectory streaming out from}
\CommentTok{ * the hovered pixel.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * Policy:}
\CommentTok{ *   {-} 30 ms debounce: never start a new integration until the pointer}
\CommentTok{ *     has been stationary for 30 ms.}
\CommentTok{ *   {-} 8 ms wall{-}clock cap per integration; on deadline, draw the}
\CommentTok{ *     partial trajectory and continue extending it on idle frames at}
\CommentTok{ *     16 ms per frame budget.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export class HoverStreamline \{}
\NormalTok{  private currentSession}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number} \OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}

  \CommentTok{/** Returns the currently displayed (possibly partial) trajectory. */}
  \FunctionTok{trajectory}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ x}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ y}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ z}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}[] \{}
\NormalTok{    return this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{lastResult}\OperatorTok{?.}\AttributeTok{trajectory} \OperatorTok{??}\NormalTok{ []}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}

  \CommentTok{/** Called by the UI on each pointer move. Decoded IC is supplied by}
\CommentTok{   *  the chart\textquotesingle{}s hover{-}decode hook. */}
  \FunctionTok{onMove}\NormalTok{(decodeIc}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ TrajState }\OperatorTok{|} \DataTypeTok{null}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{void}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{lastMoveAt} \OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ performance}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{now}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentSession}\OperatorTok{++;}
\NormalTok{    const sessionId }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentSession}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{setTimeout}\NormalTok{(() }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{maybeRun}\NormalTok{(sessionId}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ decodeIc)}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}

\NormalTok{  private }\FunctionTok{maybeRun}\NormalTok{(sessionId}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ decodeIc}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ TrajState }\OperatorTok{|} \DataTypeTok{null}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{void}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (sessionId }\OperatorTok{!==}\NormalTok{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentSession}\NormalTok{) return}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// superseded}
\NormalTok{    const ic }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{decodeIc}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{ic) return}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{    const start }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ performance}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{now}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const budget }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{8}\OperatorTok{;}
    \CommentTok{// Run a short{-}horizon inspector with a tight budget. The inspector}
    \CommentTok{// returns whatever fraction of the trajectory it managed in the}
    \CommentTok{// budget; we extend it on subsequent idle frames.}
\NormalTok{    const result }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{runInspector}\NormalTok{(ic}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ \{}
      \OperatorTok{...}\NormalTok{RK45\_DEFAULTS}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      THorizon}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{30}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      fullTrace}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ false}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      checkpointCount}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{64}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    \})}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (sessionId }\OperatorTok{!==}\NormalTok{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentSession}\NormalTok{) return}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// user moved again}
\NormalTok{    this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{lastResult} \OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{      sessionId}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      trajectory}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ result}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{nShape}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const elapsed }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ performance}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{now}\NormalTok{() }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ start}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (elapsed }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=}\NormalTok{ budget }\OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ result}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{tEnd} \OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{30}\NormalTok{) \{}
      \CommentTok{// Schedule a continuation. (M9 shows the contract; production may}
      \CommentTok{// requestIdleCallback or use the existing render{-}loop slot.)}
\NormalTok{    \}}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-7}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-7}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why two integrators.} The default RK45 is best at chasing
  near-collision singularities (its adaptive step shrinks fast as
  \texttt{r\_min} collapses). The match-integrator mode lets the user
  verify the GPU's symplectic result without integrator-family
  confusion. Spec notes are explicit about this (revision 17): comparing
  energy traces between non-symplectic RK45 and symplectic Yoshida is
  not apples-to-apples on long bounded orbits.
\item
  \textbf{Hover streamline budget.} The 8 ms cap is just a soft target;
  the real work is the debounce + session-supersession. The
  implementation here uses \texttt{setTimeout} and a session counter;
  production may swap in \texttt{requestIdleCallback} once the rest of
  the GUI exists.
\item
  \textbf{Shadow trajectory step decoupling.}
  \texttt{inspectorWithShadow} reuses the base step size for the shadow.
  Production may decouple the two for better FTLE accuracy (each can
  adapt independently); for M9 the simpler approach is enough to land
  the gate.
\item
  \textbf{Validation panel.} When the GPU \texttt{SimResult} for the
  same locked IC is available, \texttt{runInspector} accepts it as an
  optional input and populates the \texttt{validation} field. M5's tile
  cache holds the \texttt{SimResult}; the inspector reads it on lock. M9
  leaves the slot open and M12's acceptance gate uses it for the spec §7
  check.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{m10-chart-instantiations}{%
\chapter{M10 --- Chart instantiations}\label{m10-chart-instantiations}}

\hypertarget{goal-10}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-10}}

Promote charts from a hard-coded latent slice (M3) to a registered set
of chart objects, each with three operations: \texttt{decode(uv)},
\texttt{inverseEncode(ic)}, \texttt{validate(uv)}. The GPU compute
shader stays chart-agnostic --- it reads \texttt{(m\_i,\ r\_i,\ p\_i)}
regardless of which chart produced them.

After M10: latent affine slice, \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)},
\texttt{(L\_z,\ K)}, shape sphere with hover streamline, ternary mass
plot, mixed-axis factory, all wired through the \texttt{chartRegistry}.
Each chart declares its compatibility flags
(\texttt{forbids\_energy\_normalisation},
\texttt{has\_redundant\_hemisphere},
\texttt{requires\_per\_pixel\_mass}) so the validation pass and the
integration shader can react.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/charts}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Every registered chart's \texttt{Φ} is total on \texttt{{[}0,\ 1{]}²}
(no NaN, every pixel either ok or terminal). Lock at the
equilateral-triangle pixel in the shape-sphere chart, switch to
\texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} chart at \texttt{K\ =\ 0}: lands at the
feasibility-parabola apex \texttt{(L\_z\ =\ 0,\ E\ =\ U)}. The
mass-simplex chart respects the interior buffer at every corner.

\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ Chart}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ ChartView \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}../types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Triple \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/math/types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Shape{-}sphere chart: the rendering surface and the dynamical state space}
\CommentTok{ * coincide. Each pixel is a point (θ, φ) on S²; the realisation map}
\CommentTok{ * recovers the canonical Jacobi (α, β) and decodes through the shared}
\CommentTok{ * pipeline.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * The chart sets \textasciigrave{}has\_redundant\_hemisphere = true\textasciigrave{}: φ ∈ (π, 2π) is the}
\CommentTok{ * reflection{-}equivalent copy of φ ∈ (0, π).}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export const shapeSphereChart}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Chart }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  id}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}shape\_sphere\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}sphere\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  flags}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ FLAGS\_SPHERE}\OperatorTok{,}

  \FunctionTok{decode}\NormalTok{([u}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ v]}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ view) \{}
\NormalTok{    const eps   }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{chartParams}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{poleBuffer} \ImportTok{as} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{??} \FloatTok{0.05}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const theta }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ eps }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ (}\BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI} \OperatorTok{{-}} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{eps) }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const phi   }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{*} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI} \OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ v}\OperatorTok{;}

    \CommentTok{// Realisation map: (θ, φ) → (α, β).}
    \CommentTok{// With the corrected shape{-}sphere formula:}
    \CommentTok{//   n\_3 = cos θ = 2 (ρ̃ × λ̃)\_z / I   →  involves both α and β}
    \CommentTok{// We use the inversion derived in the spec revision:}
    \CommentTok{//   2α = arccos({-}sin θ cos φ)}
    \CommentTok{//   β = atan2(cos θ, {-}sin θ sin φ), folded into [0, π].}
\NormalTok{    const sinT }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sin}\NormalTok{(theta)}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ cosT }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{cos}\NormalTok{(theta)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const cosPhi }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{cos}\NormalTok{(phi)}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ sinPhi }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sin}\NormalTok{(phi)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const alpha }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{acos}\NormalTok{(}\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{sinT }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ cosPhi) }\OperatorTok{/} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    let beta }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{atan2}\NormalTok{(cosT}\OperatorTok{,} \OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{sinT }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ sinPhi)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (beta }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) beta }\OperatorTok{+=} \DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{*} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (beta }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI}\NormalTok{) beta }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{*} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI} \OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ beta}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// hemisphere fold}

\NormalTok{    const m }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{m} \OperatorTok{??}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const muRho    }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (m[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{m[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]) }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ (m[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{m[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const muLambda }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ m[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ (m[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{m[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{])}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const rho}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{    Vec2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{cos}\NormalTok{(alpha) }\OperatorTok{/} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sqrt}\NormalTok{(muRho)}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const lambda}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Vec2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ [}\BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sin}\NormalTok{(alpha) }\OperatorTok{*} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{cos}\NormalTok{(beta) }\OperatorTok{/} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sqrt}\NormalTok{(muLambda)}\OperatorTok{,}
                          \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sin}\NormalTok{(alpha) }\OperatorTok{*} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sin}\NormalTok{(beta) }\OperatorTok{/} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sqrt}\NormalTok{(muLambda)]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const r}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Triple}\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{Vec2}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{jacobiToParticlePositions}\NormalTok{(rho}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ lambda}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ m)}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{    const pRho}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{    Vec2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{chartParams}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{pRho}    \ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ Vec2) }\OperatorTok{??}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const pLambda}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Vec2 }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (view}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{chartParams}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{pLambda} \ImportTok{as}\NormalTok{ Vec2) }\OperatorTok{??}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    const p}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Triple}\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{Vec2}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{jacobiToParticleMomenta}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{      \{ pRho}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ pLambda \} }\ImportTok{as} \DataTypeTok{any}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    )}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{    const c }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{canonicalise}\NormalTok{(\{ r}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ p}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ t}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{                           \{ deltaLambda}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ EPS\_DEADBAND}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ rColl}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ R\_COLL\_DEFAULT \})}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{terminal}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{      return \{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}terminal\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ terminal}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{terminal}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{               descriptor}\OperatorTok{:} \FunctionTok{makeStubDescriptor}\NormalTok{(m) \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    \}}
\NormalTok{    return \{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}ok\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ state}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{state}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ descriptor}\OperatorTok{:} \FunctionTok{makeStubDescriptor}\NormalTok{(m) \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}

  \FunctionTok{inverseEncode}\NormalTok{(ic) \{}
\NormalTok{    return \{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}projected\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reason}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}shape\_sphere inverse not unique without chart params\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}

  \FunctionTok{validate}\NormalTok{([u}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ v]) \{}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (u }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{0} \OperatorTok{||}\NormalTok{ u }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{1} \OperatorTok{||}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{0} \OperatorTok{||}\NormalTok{ v }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{) \{}

\NormalTok{    \}}
    \CommentTok{// Pole buffer is enforced via theta(u) so no further check needed.}
\NormalTok{    return \{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}pass\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{\}}\OperatorTok{;}

\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{makeStubDescriptor}\NormalTok{(m}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{any}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{any}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  return \{ m}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ qMass}\OperatorTok{:} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{min}\NormalTok{(}\OperatorTok{...}\NormalTok{m)}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{           rho1Mag}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ rho2Mag}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ rhoRatio}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ rhoAngle}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{           K0}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ V0}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ virial}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ rMinPair0}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{;}

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-8}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-8}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Chart registry is the single dispatch point.} The renderer
  asks for \texttt{getChart(view.chartType)} and never branches on the
  chart kind. This is what keeps the GPU shader chart-agnostic: the WGSL
  only consumes \texttt{(m\_i,\ r\_i,\ p\_i)}.
\item
  \textbf{The \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} chart's α and β are frozen by the
  caller via \texttt{chartParams}.} M11's Burrau ternary plot supplies
  them per pixel, not the chart itself; the chart contract is just
  ``what does \texttt{(L\_z,\ K(t))} decode to given the surrounding
  configuration?''. This keeps the chart factory composable.
\item
  \textbf{Mixed-axis is intentionally partial.} Latent × latent ships;
  mass × \{anything else\} and shape × \{anything else\} land in M11 and
  M12 alongside their respective acceptance tests. The contract is
  locked here so M11 / M12 can extend without touching the registry.
\item
  \textbf{The chart's \texttt{wgsl} field} is reserved for
  chart-specific WGSL fragments that get inlined into the GPU dispatch.
  M10 doesn't ship any yet --- every chart so far decodes to
  \texttt{(m,\ r,\ p)} on the CPU and lets the GPU integrator run
  unchanged. M11's hover-streamline integration may need a
  chart-specific sphere mapping in the fragment shader, which is where
  this hook becomes useful.
\item
  \textbf{Validation policy.} \texttt{compatible()} covers the
  energy-normalisation-vs-invariant-chart case. M12's acceptance pass
  enforces it for every export configuration.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{m11-burrau-family-progression}{%
\chapter{M11 --- Burrau family
progression}\label{m11-burrau-family-progression}}

\hypertarget{goal-11}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-11}}

The Burrau--Pythagorean family as a layered traversal of the IC
manifold, each stage adding one degree of freedom. The progression rides
on top of M10's chart machinery: every Burrau view is a \texttt{Chart}
configured with specific frozen parameters, no Burrau-specific
integrator or renderer.

After M11: discrete primitive triples at rest (Stage 1a), continuous
\texttt{ν} sweep (Stage 1b), continuous masses at fixed shape (Stage
2a), continuous \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} at fixed shape and masses (Stage
2b), combined mass + momentum sweeps (Stage 3), and the Stage 4
persistence probe --- locking on a fractal Burrau boundary and tilting
one basis vector into a non-Burrau direction.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/burrau\_family}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The (3, 4, 5) classical IC reproduces the M1 golden after going through
the full chart pipeline (lookup → decode → integrate). The first four
primitive triples produce distinct geometries. Stage 4 persistence probe
runs cleanly: lock + tilt sweep produces a smooth
\texttt{coherence\_score} trace.

\hypertarget{srcburraueuclid.ts}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/burrau/euclid.ts}}{src/burrau/euclid.ts}}\label{srcburraueuclid.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ Vec2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Vec3}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ Triple \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/math/types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Continuous Euclid parametrisation. For real m \textgreater{} n \textgreater{} 0 the formulae}
\CommentTok{ *   a = m² {-} n²,  b = 2 m n,  c = m² + n²}
\CommentTok{ * give a Pythagorean{-}style triple with a² + b² = c² for any m, n.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * The single ratio ν = n / m ∈ (0, 1) determines the triangle shape;}
\CommentTok{ * \textasciigrave{}m\textasciigrave{} itself sets the absolute scale (irrelevant after the I = 1 gauge).}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{euclidSides}\NormalTok{(m}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ n}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ a}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ b}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \} \{}
\NormalTok{  return \{ a}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{m }\OperatorTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ n}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{n}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ b}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{m}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{n}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{m }\OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ n}\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{n \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{/** Normalised by m² so a, b, c depend only on ν. */}

\CommentTok{/**}

\CommentTok{ * the per{-}tilt summary so the caller can plot persistence.}

\CommentTok{ * from the GPU dispatcher.}

\NormalTok{  pixel}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ s}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ t}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  tiltTarget}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  steps}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}

\NormalTok{    outcome\_impurity}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    coherence\_score}\OperatorTok{:}  \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    word}\OperatorTok{?:}            \DataTypeTok{string}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{},}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \BuiltInTok{Promise}\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{PersistenceTracePoint[]}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}

\NormalTok{      coherenceScore}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  summary}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{coherence\_score}\OperatorTok{,}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ Chart \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/chart\_atlas/types.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{ makeThetaKStrip}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ makeThetaDeltaMStrip \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./bifurcation.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * The Stage 1a → 4 escalation, materialised as concrete \textasciigrave{}Chart\textasciigrave{} objects}
\CommentTok{ * keyed by stage. The renderer / tile dispatcher reads these directly.}
\CommentTok{ */}

  \CommentTok{/** Stage 1a: discrete primitive triples at rest. Just a UI layer over}
\CommentTok{   *  the Euclid display chart with a small landmark list. */}
  \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1a\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    chart}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ burrauEuclidChart}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    landmarks}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}(3,4,5)\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}(5,12,13)\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}(15,8,17)\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}(7,24,25)\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}

  \CommentTok{/** Stage 1b: continuous ν sweep. Same chart, no landmarks pinned. */}
  \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}1b\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ chart}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ burrauEuclidChart}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ landmarks}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [] }\ImportTok{as} \DataTypeTok{string}\NormalTok{[] \}}\OperatorTok{,}

  \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}2b\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ lzEChart}\OperatorTok{,}

  \CommentTok{/** Stage 3 (combined): mass × kinetic{-}energy strip. */}
  \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}3\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{:} \FunctionTok{makeThetaDeltaMStrip}\NormalTok{(\{ mTarget}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{] \})}\OperatorTok{,}

  \CommentTok{/** Stage 4: full 8D — handled at the interaction layer via tilt}
\CommentTok{   *  sweeps. The probe lives in \textasciigrave{}hypothesis\_probe.ts\textasciigrave{}. */}

\hypertarget{acceptance-check-11}{%
\section{Acceptance check}\label{acceptance-check-11}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/burrau\_family}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Two goldens green: the (3, 4, 5) classical IC produced by the Euclid
parametrisation reproduces the M1 outcome (escape, body 1) with energy
drift below 1e-7; the persistence probe runs cleanly over 30 steps and
yields a smooth trace.

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-9}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-9}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Stage 4 wiring.} \texttt{probePersistence} accepts an injected
  \texttt{tileSummary} function so it works in tests without the GPU. In
  production, the function dispatches a one-shot tile compute (the tile
  centred on the locked pixel at the smallest depth), reads back the
  \texttt{TileReduction}, and returns the relevant fields. M5's
  \texttt{planFrame} already handles the dispatch.
\item
  \textbf{Mass-axis charts and \texttt{requires\_per\_pixel\_mass}.}
  Stage 2a, Stage 3, and the (θ, δm) strip all set this flag. The
  integration shader (M3 + M6) already reads \texttt{m\_i} from
  \texttt{ICDescriptor} per pixel rather than from
  \texttt{SimUniforms.m{[}3{]}}, so no change is needed at this
  milestone --- but the flag exists so dispatchers can refuse fixed-mass
  shortcuts in Burrau-family contexts.
\item
  \textbf{Burrau Jacobi vector convention.} The classical Burrau
  labelling (1-indexed: body 1 at right angle) is preserved inside
  \texttt{euclid.ts} only to make formulae easy to compare with the
  literature. Every emitted \texttt{(m,\ r)} is already 0-indexed for
  the rest of the pipeline.
\item
  \textbf{Acute angle range.} The chart maps θ ∈ (0, π/4{]}. θ = 0 is
  the degenerate limit ν → 1 (isoceles right triangle's mirror); θ = π/4
  is ν → 0 (degenerate elongated triangle). The chart's small
  \texttt{theta\_min} buffer keeps both ends finite.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{m12-export-data-api-acceptance-harness}{%
\chapter{M12 --- Export, data API, acceptance
harness}\label{m12-export-data-api-acceptance-harness}}

\hypertarget{goal-12}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-12}}

The exit milestone. Make every parameter that affects rendering or
computation reachable from a serialisable \texttt{ViewState}, hang every
non-interactive workflow off it (URL sharing, single-frame export,
animated sweep, live simulation, data export), and wire the spec §7
acceptance gates into CI so regressions caught here block merging.

After M12: \texttt{ViewState} is the canonical schema; URL sharing
round-trips losslessly; static exports produce flat
\texttt{SimResult{[}W×H{]}} buffers with optional sub-buffer
partitioning when \texttt{maxStorageBufferBindingSize} is exceeded;
animated exports interpret a \texttt{Timeline} of keyframe tracks with
seven easing functions; data exports produce PNG / JSON / binary / CSV /
NPZ; reproducibility sidecars carry the full state plus a SHA-256 hash
of the binary payload.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/acceptance}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

All six spec §7 architectural checks pass on the frozen corpus: - Spec
A1: \texttt{n(t)} storage is stable near poles and wrap regions. - Spec
A2: tiles marked coherent stay visually and dynamically coherent one
level deeper. - Spec A3: coarse baseline coverage stays available while
children are pending. - Spec A4: changing render mode does not change
the compute payload. - Spec A5: \texttt{FTLE\_VALID} outputs only appear
when Benettin renormalisation ran. - Spec A6: bounded-trajectory energy
drift is below threshold.

Additionally: a 10-frame \texttt{z{[}3{]}} sweep round-trips
byte-for-byte through the sidecar reproducibility check.

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{partitionBuffer}\NormalTok{(}

\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ SubBufferPlan[] \{}

\NormalTok{              byteOffset}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ byteSize}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ totalBytes \}]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}

\NormalTok{      byteSize}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{   rows }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ width }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ bytesPerSample}\OperatorTok{,}

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-10}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-10}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{ViewState} discipline.} Every UI control, every cache
  key, every exported sidecar consumes the same object. Adding a new
  control means: add the field to \texttt{ViewState}, propagate to
  \texttt{viewStateToCacheKey} if the field affects compute, and write a
  default in \texttt{defaultViewState}. M12's URL/timeline/sidecar
  machinery picks it up for free.
\item
  \textbf{Binary format versioning.} The 1-byte version field in
  \texttt{encodeBinary} is the on-disk schema version. Any future change
  to \texttt{SimResult} field order or width that's not absorbed by
  \texttt{payload\_version} (M5's cache key) bumps this and forces
  consumers to switch readers.
\item
  \textbf{Acceptance tests are layered.} A1 is a unit-pass test; A2
  needs M5; A3 needs M4; A4 needs M7; A5 needs M6; A6 needs M1. Each
  test imports what it needs and stays as small as possible --- the goal
  is ``fast, determinative, regressable'', not ``full coverage of every
  code path''.
\item
  \textbf{NPZ has a real platform dependency.} The contract here is
  enough for M12's gate; the actual NumPy-zip writer
  (e.g.~\texttt{numjs} or a purpose-built one) lands at deployment time.
  The pipeline declines to write NPZ when the dependency isn't loaded,
  falling back to the binary format with a console warning.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{g1-shader-composition-wgsl-linker}{%
\chapter{G1 --- Shader composition / WGSL
linker}\label{g1-shader-composition-wgsl-linker}}

\hypertarget{goal-13}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-13}}

A real cross-shader composition layer. M3, M5, M6 all ship WGSL
fragments that reference each other (\texttt{mass\_softmax} from
\texttt{helpers.wgsl} is called by \texttt{decode.wgsl};
\texttt{shape\_sphere} from \texttt{metrics.wgsl} is called by
\texttt{simulate.wgsl}); the milestones used a stub
\texttt{concatShaders()} to glue them, which is fragile and produces
silent symbol clashes.

After G1: a \texttt{wgslLink} function that resolves
\texttt{//\ @import} directives, flattens the dependency graph,
validates that every referenced symbol is either defined locally or
imported, and emits one syntactically-valid shader module per pipeline.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/shader\_compose}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The simulate, reduce, and render pipelines all produce valid WGSL
modules that pass \texttt{device.createShaderModule} without warnings on
Chrome's WebGPU implementation. A symbol used but not defined produces a
loud error at link time, with line/file context, before reaching the
GPU.

\hypertarget{file-tree-12}{%
\section{File tree}\label{file-tree-12}}

\begin{verbatim}
principia/
  src/
    gpu/
      wgsl/
        link.ts                 # the linker
        parse_imports.ts        # @import directive parser
        symbol_index.ts         # function/struct/const declaration index
        validate.ts             # symbol resolution check
        format_error.ts         # human-readable link errors
      shaders/
        helpers.wgsl            # @export everything that's reused
        decode.wgsl             # @import { mass_softmax } from helpers
        integrate.wgsl
        events.wgsl
        observe.wgsl
        metrics.wgsl
        simulate.wgsl
        reduce.wgsl
        render_layer0.wgsl
  test/
    unit/gpu/wgsl/
      parse_imports.test.ts
      symbol_index.test.ts
      validate.test.ts
      link.test.ts
    integration/
      shader_compose.test.ts
\end{verbatim}

\hypertarget{import-directive-syntax}{%
\section{Import directive syntax}\label{import-directive-syntax}}

A line-comment that starts with \texttt{//\ @import} declares cross-file
dependencies. Three forms:

\begin{verbatim}
// @import { mass_softmax, sigmoid } from "./helpers.wgsl"
// @import * as helpers from "./helpers.wgsl"
// @import "./helpers.wgsl"               // brings in everything @export'ed
\end{verbatim}

\texttt{@export} marks a top-level symbol as importable. Anything not
exported is module-private. The convention matches ES modules
deliberately; it keeps mental model overhead low.

\begin{verbatim}
// @export
fn mass_softmax(z1: f32, z2: f32, mu_max: f32) -> vec3<f32> { ... }

// @export
struct State { /* ... */ }
\end{verbatim}

\CommentTok{/**}

\CommentTok{ * imports and the set of symbols this file exports.}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{parseDirectives}\NormalTok{(src}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{string}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{}

\NormalTok{        symbols}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!.}\FunctionTok{split}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{},\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{map}\NormalTok{(s }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{trim}\NormalTok{())}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(Boolean)}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        fromPath}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!,}
\NormalTok{        line}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{    \}}

\NormalTok{      imports}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{push}\NormalTok{(\{ kind}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}namespace\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ alias}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ fromPath}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ m[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!,}\NormalTok{ line}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{ \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/** Validate that every named import points at a real export, and that}

\hypertarget{how-m3-m5-m6-m7-shaders-look-after-g1}{%
\section{How M3 / M5 / M6 / M7 shaders look after
G1}\label{how-m3-m5-m6-m7-shaders-look-after-g1}}

\hypertarget{helpers.wgsl}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{helpers.wgsl}}{helpers.wgsl}}\label{helpers.wgsl}}

\begin{verbatim}
// @export
fn sigmoid(z: f32) -> f32 {
  if (z >= 0.0) { return 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-z)); }
  let e = exp(z);  return e / (1.0 + e);
}

// @export
fn mass_softmax(z1: f32, z2: f32, mu_max: f32) -> vec3<f32> {
  // ...
}

// @export
fn rotJ(v: vec2<f32>) -> vec2<f32> { return vec2<f32>(-v.y, v.x); }
\end{verbatim}

Linker produces topologically-ordered, directive-free WGSL. Cycles and
unresolved symbols fail loudly at link time, not silently at GPU compile
time.

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-11}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-11}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{One-directory-only rule.} \texttt{resolveImport} rejects
  \texttt{..} and \texttt{/}; all shaders live in
  \texttt{src/gpu/shaders/}. Keeps the linker tiny and the module graph
  easy to reason about.
\item
  \textbf{Bundler integration.} The Vite / esbuild glue uses
  \texttt{?raw} imports to read each \texttt{.wgsl} file as text at
  build time. The linker doesn't read from disk --- it just consumes
  \texttt{Record\textless{}path,\ source\textgreater{}}. This keeps it
  testable and lets you swap in a different IO mechanism (e.g.
  hot-reload from a watcher).
\item
  \textbf{Future room.} The directive grammar is deliberately
  restrictive (matches ES modules at the syntactic level). If you ever
  need conditional compilation or per-tier specialisation, the natural
  extension is to add \texttt{//\ @if\ FTLE\_ENABLED} /
  \texttt{//\ @endif} blocks; the parser is small enough that this is a
  30-line addition.
\item
  \textbf{No re-exports.} A unit can't \texttt{//\ @export\ \{\ foo\ \}}
  something it imported. If you need that, write a wrapper function.
  Keeping the rule means \texttt{validateImports} is local; otherwise it
  has to do fixed-point analysis.
\item
  \textbf{Compilation info.} Browsers expose
  \texttt{module.getCompilationInfo()} for shader warnings; the
  integration test above uses it when available. CI pipelines that run a
  real headless Chrome can flag warnings as test failures.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{g2-frame-loop-and-orchestration}{%
\chapter{G2 --- Frame loop and
orchestration}\label{g2-frame-loop-and-orchestration}}

\hypertarget{goal-14}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-14}}

The top-level \texttt{App} class that owns the per-frame schedule. After
G2, the milestone graph has a ``main'' --- every other milestone is
something this loop calls into.

The loop: 1. Reads \texttt{ViewState} from the reactive store. 2.
Collects the visible tile frontier at the desired depth. 3. Walks
ancestors for any missing tile (so the screen never blanks). 4. Plans
this frame's compute jobs via M5's \texttt{planFrame}. 5. Dispatches GPU
compute + reduction passes; ingests reductions on completion. 6. Renders
the frontier with M7's render graph. 7. Handles input events: chart
switches, lock, tilt, lookup, palette.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/app\_frame\_loop}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

A 100-frame synthetic harness (mocked GPU dispatch) drives the loop
through: a pan, a zoom step, a chart switch, a lock and inspect, a
palette swap. Every frame produces a valid render plan; the cache hits
the expected hit rate; reductions are ingested in submission order; no
tile is dispatched twice; the inspector recomputes once on lock and no
more.

\NormalTok{  cancel}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{   (id}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{) }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}} \DataTypeTok{void}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{/** Pluggable GPU dispatcher. Real impl wires through M3 / M5. */}

\CommentTok{   *  resolves with the tile\textquotesingle{}s TileReduction. The same promise resolves}
\CommentTok{   *  even if the tile scrolls offscreen — the caller drops the result. */}
  \FunctionTok{dispatchTile}\NormalTok{(tileId}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TileID}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ view}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ViewState)}\OperatorTok{:} \BuiltInTok{Promise}\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{TileReduction}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{};}

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-12}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-12}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why a class, not a function.} The frame loop holds long-lived
  state (the cache, the in-flight ledger, the rAF id) across many
  invocations. A class makes the lifecycle explicit; tests can call
  \texttt{tickOnce()} deterministically without driving the rAF
  schedule.
\item
  \textbf{Single source of truth.} Every entry-point method on
  \texttt{App} reads or writes via \texttt{Store}. The loop never sees
  its own private state of the world. This makes the URL-share /
  sidecar-reproduce path in M12 work without surgery.
\item
  \textbf{Inspector lifecycle.} Crafting a clean lock-on-pixel UX needs
  three signals: lock fired (kick the inspector), unlock fired (drop the
  promise), chart-switch fired (preserve or refuse). The store's
  subscribe callback owns all three.
\item
  \textbf{Cancellation model.} WebGPU dispatches cannot be aborted, so
  cancellation is logical: \texttt{cancelOffscreen} marks the in-flight
  job's result as discardable. The job still runs; its reduction is
  dropped by the \texttt{if\ (job.cancelled)\ return} guard. Eviction in
  the cache reclaims the memory.
\item
  \textbf{Frame-budget tuning.} \texttt{frameBudget:\ 16} (in
  tile-jobs/frame, not ms) is a reasonable starting point for
  \texttt{N\ =\ 16}, \texttt{T\_horizon\ =\ 80}. Real perf work tunes by
  tier: Preview lifts to 32, Research drops to 8.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{g3-bind-group-layout-authority}{%
\chapter{G3 --- Bind-group layout
authority}\label{g3-bind-group-layout-authority}}

\hypertarget{goal-15}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-15}}

A single \texttt{Layouts} module that all three pipelines (simulate,
reduce, render) consume. M3, M5, and M7 each define their own bind-group
layouts; in real WebGPU, sharing pre-bound bind groups across pipelines
requires the layout objects to be the same identity (not just
structurally equivalent). Without G3, you get
\texttt{GPUValidationError:\ bind\ group\ at\ index\ N\ is\ not\ compatible}
the first time you try to bind a SimResult buffer for both compute and
render.

After G3: one \texttt{buildLayouts(device)} call returns the canonical
\texttt{PipelineLayouts} object; all three pipelines use it; bind groups
allocated for one pipeline bind cleanly into the others.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/layout\_compat}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The same \texttt{BindGroup} object created for the simulate pipeline
binds without validation errors when used in the reduce pipeline (input
group), the render pipeline (storage read), and the inspector preview
pipeline.

\hypertarget{file-tree-14}{%
\section{File tree}\label{file-tree-14}}

\begin{verbatim}
principia/
  src/
    gpu/
      layouts.ts                # the single source of truth
      pipelines/
        simulate.ts             # M3 dispatch, refactored to consume Layouts
        reduce.ts               # M5
        render.ts               # M7
        inspector_preview.ts    # M9 hover-streamline
      buffers.ts                # extended to expose canonical bind groups
  test/
    unit/gpu/
      layouts.test.ts
    integration/
      layout_compat.test.ts
\end{verbatim}

\hypertarget{srcgpulayouts.ts}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/layouts.ts}}{src/gpu/layouts.ts}}\label{srcgpulayouts.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Canonical bind{-}group layouts. Every pipeline in Principia must use}
\CommentTok{ * these layout objects (not equivalent ad{-}hoc instances), so that bind}
\CommentTok{ * groups allocated against any one of them rebind cleanly across all.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * Group structure:}
\CommentTok{ *   group(0): frame{-}level uniforms — SimUniforms + TileRequest +}
\CommentTok{ *             ChartUniforms (the last one is added by G4).}
\CommentTok{ *   group(1): per{-}tile storage — SimResult and ICDescriptor.}
\CommentTok{ *   group(2): per{-}tile reduction output — TileReduction.}
\CommentTok{ *   group(3): render{-}only uniforms — RenderParams.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * Visibility flags are the union of every stage that needs the binding;}
\CommentTok{ * WebGPU validation is fine with overspecification, and this lets the}
\CommentTok{ * same layout object back compute{-}only and fragment{-}also pipelines.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export interface PipelineLayouts \{}
  \CommentTok{/** group 0 */}\NormalTok{ frame}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{    GPUBindGroupLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** group 1 */}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  GPUBindGroupLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** group 2 */}\NormalTok{ reduction}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{GPUBindGroupLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** group 3 */}\NormalTok{ render}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{   GPUBindGroupLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** Composite layouts for each pipeline. */}
\NormalTok{  pipelineSimulate}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{        GPUPipelineLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  pipelineReduce}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{          GPUPipelineLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  pipelineRender}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{          GPUPipelineLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  pipelineInspectorPreview}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{GPUPipelineLayout}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{buildLayouts}\NormalTok{(device}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUDevice)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ PipelineLayouts \{}
\NormalTok{  const FRAGMENT\_AND\_COMPUTE }\OperatorTok{=}
\NormalTok{    GPUShaderStage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{COMPUTE} \OperatorTok{|}\NormalTok{ GPUShaderStage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{FRAGMENT}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  const frame }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroupLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.frame\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ FRAGMENT\_AND\_COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}uniform\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// SimUniforms}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUShaderStage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}uniform\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// TileRequest}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ FRAGMENT\_AND\_COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}uniform\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// ChartUniforms (G4)}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  const perTile }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroupLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.perTile\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ FRAGMENT\_AND\_COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
        \CommentTok{// \textquotesingle{}read{-}only{-}storage\textquotesingle{} is binding{-}compatible with a \textquotesingle{}storage\textquotesingle{}}
        \CommentTok{// group that holds the same buffer in another pipeline. We use}
        \CommentTok{// \textquotesingle{}storage\textquotesingle{} here because the simulate compute writes to it.}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}storage\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// SimResult}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ FRAGMENT\_AND\_COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}storage\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// ICDescriptor}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  const reduction }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroupLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.reduction\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUShaderStage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{COMPUTE}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}storage\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// TileReduction}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  const render }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroupLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.render\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ visibility}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUShaderStage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{FRAGMENT}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{        buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ type}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}uniform\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}                     \CommentTok{// RenderParams}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  const pipelineSimulate }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createPipelineLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.pipeline.simulate\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    bindGroupLayouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const pipelineReduce }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createPipelineLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.pipeline.reduce\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
    \CommentTok{// Reduce reads perTile (storage) and writes reduction (storage).}
\NormalTok{    bindGroupLayouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduction]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const pipelineRender }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createPipelineLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.pipeline.render\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
    \CommentTok{// Render reads frame, perTile (storage as readonly), and render.}
\NormalTok{    bindGroupLayouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduction}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ render]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const pipelineInspectorPreview }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createPipelineLayout}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.pipeline.inspectorPreview\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    bindGroupLayouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduction}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ render]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  return \{}
\NormalTok{    frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduction}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ render}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    pipelineSimulate}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ pipelineReduce}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    pipelineRender}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ pipelineInspectorPreview}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\hypertarget{why-a-single-source-of-truth-matters}{%
\section{Why a single source of truth
matters}\label{why-a-single-source-of-truth-matters}}

WebGPU's bind-group compatibility check is identity-based, not
structural. Two \texttt{GPUBindGroupLayout} objects that have the same
descriptor are \emph{not} interchangeable. If M3's compute pipeline
binds a SimResult buffer to its own layout, that bind group can't be
passed to M7's render pipeline that uses an equivalent-but-distinct
layout --- WebGPU throws
\texttt{bind\ group\ at\ index\ 1\ is\ not\ compatible}.

Real implementations have hit this with shared cross-pipeline buffers.
The fix is to centralise.

\hypertarget{how-m3-m5-m7-change}{%
\section{How M3 / M5 / M7 change}\label{how-m3-m5-m7-change}}

Each pipeline-construction file becomes a thin wrapper around the
canonical layouts. Below: the M3 \texttt{dispatch\_layer0.ts} redux.

\hypertarget{bind-group-construction-also-centralised}{%
\section{Bind-group construction (also
centralised)}\label{bind-group-construction-also-centralised}}

Tiles allocate bind groups once at compute-time and reuse them on every
subsequent render. The helper:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{// src/gpu/buffers.ts (extension)}
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ PipelineLayouts \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./layouts.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ TileBuffers \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./buffers.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{export interface TileBindGroups \{}
  \CommentTok{/** group(0) — frame{-}level uniforms. Bound once per frame. */}
\NormalTok{  frame}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{     GPUBindGroup}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** group(1) — per{-}tile storage. Bound once per tile. */}
\NormalTok{  perTile}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{   GPUBindGroup}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** group(2) — per{-}tile reduction output. Bound during the reduce pass. */}
\NormalTok{  reduction}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBindGroup}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{createTileBindGroups}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  ctx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ device}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUDevice \}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ PipelineLayouts}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  bufs}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TileBuffers}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ chartUniforms}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBuffer}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reductionBuffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBuffer}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TileBindGroups \{}
\NormalTok{  const frame }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroup}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.bg.frame\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    layout}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{frame}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{uniforms}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{tileReq}\NormalTok{  \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ chartUniforms \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}        \CommentTok{// G4}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const perTile }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroup}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.bg.perTile\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    layout}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{perTile}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{simResults}\NormalTok{ \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{icDesc}\NormalTok{     \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const reduction }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroup}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.bg.reduction\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    layout}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{reduction}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}
\NormalTok{      \{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ reductionBuffer \} \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    ]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  return \{ frame}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ perTile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduction \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The render-only group(3) (\texttt{RenderParams}) lives separately
because swapping it shouldn't touch the per-tile bind group:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{createRenderParamsBindGroup}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  ctx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ device}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUDevice \}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ PipelineLayouts}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ paramsBuffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBuffer}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBindGroup \{}
\NormalTok{  return ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBindGroup}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    label}\OperatorTok{:} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}principia.bg.renderParams\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    layout}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{render}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    entries}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [\{ binding}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ resource}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ buffer}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ paramsBuffer \} \}]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\hypertarget{tests-15}{%
\section{Tests}\label{tests-15}}

\hypertarget{testunitgpulayouts.test.ts}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{test/unit/gpu/layouts.test.ts}}{test/unit/gpu/layouts.test.ts}}\label{testunitgpulayouts.test.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{ describe}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ it}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ expect \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}vitest\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Layout descriptor shapes are stable. We can\textquotesingle{}t construct a}
\CommentTok{ * GPUBindGroupLayout in a unit test, but we can test the descriptors}
\CommentTok{ * directly via a thin export.}
\CommentTok{ */}

\CommentTok{// In real code, expose the descriptor objects (not just the layouts) so}
\CommentTok{// tests can introspect.}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  FRAME\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ PER\_TILE\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  REDUCTION\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ RENDER\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{\} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/gpu/layouts.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\FunctionTok{describe}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}layout descriptors\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
  \FunctionTok{it}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}frame group has SimUniforms (0), TileRequest (1), ChartUniforms (2)\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(FRAME\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{entries}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toHaveLength}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(FRAME\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{entries}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!.}\AttributeTok{binding}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBe}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(FRAME\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{entries}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!.}\AttributeTok{binding}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBe}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{expect}\NormalTok{(FRAME\_LAYOUT\_DESC}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{entries}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!.}\AttributeTok{binding}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{toBe}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}

  \FunctionTok{it}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}frame.SimUniforms is visible to compute and fragment\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
