\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-13}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-13}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Visibility unions.} Each binding's \texttt{visibility} flag is
  the union of every stage the binding is read in. The simulate compute
  writes the SimResult buffer; the render fragment reads it; both flags
  must appear, even though only one runs at a time. This is per-binding,
  not per-pipeline --- a bind group satisfies a layout iff every entry's
  declared visibility covers its actual use.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{storage} vs \texttt{read-only-storage}.} The simulate
  pipeline writes the SimResult buffer (storage). The render pipeline
  only reads it. WebGPU lets a pipeline declare
  \texttt{read-only-storage} while the bind group's underlying buffer
  was created with \texttt{STORAGE} usage, but the layout entry types
  must match exactly across the pipelines that share the bind group. We
  use \texttt{storage} (read-write) at the layout level and let the
  render shader treat it as read-only via
  \texttt{var\textless{}storage,\ read\textgreater{}}. Validation
  passes.
\item
  \textbf{Render-only group(3)} stays separate so that palette swaps and
  CVD-mode toggles only rebind one group (the one with
  \texttt{RenderParams}), leaving the per-tile and frame groups intact.
\item
  \textbf{Pipeline labels.} All \texttt{label:} strings flow through to
  the browser's GPU validation messages. Worth keeping; debugging
  validation errors is much easier with named layouts.
\item
  \textbf{Future room.} When G4 adds \texttt{ChartUniforms} and G7 adds
  the ensemble dispatch, the layout doesn't need to change --- both ride
  on existing slots. Resist the urge to add new groups; the stable shape
  here is part of the architectural contract.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{g4-chart-parameter-promotion}{%
\chapter{G4 --- Chart-parameter
promotion}\label{g4-chart-parameter-promotion}}

\hypertarget{goal-16}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-16}}

Move the decoder hyperparameters (\texttt{mu\_max}, \texttt{alpha\_min},
\texttt{q\_max}, \texttt{r\_coll}, \texttt{delta\_lambda}, plus
chart-specific things like \texttt{Kmax}, \texttt{gamma\_K},
\texttt{pole\_buffer}) out of \texttt{SimUniforms} and into a per-chart
\texttt{ChartUniforms} buffer that the shader reads alongside.

In M3 these knobs were hard-coded into \texttt{SimUniforms} as a stopgap
--- fine for the latent slice, fine for the M3 gate, immediately wrong
as soon as M10's chart system tries to vary them per chart. G4 fixes it.

After G4: the chart registry is the source of truth for chart
parameters, and the same shader runs every chart unchanged because the
chart-specific knobs come in via group(0) binding(2) --- not via
specialisation constants, not via shader recompilation.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/chart\_uniforms}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Switching from the latent slice (default α\_min = 0.05) to a custom
chart (α\_min = 0.20) does not trigger a shader recompile; the
\texttt{ChartUniforms} buffer rebinds and the next dispatch reads the
new values.

\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/chart\_uniforms.ts}}{src/gpu/chart\_uniforms.ts}}\label{srcgpuchart_uniforms.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * ChartUniforms is bound at group(0) binding(2). 64 bytes, vec4{-}aligned.}
\CommentTok{ * Layout reserved a few slots for chart{-}specific parameters; future}
\CommentTok{ * charts that need more can pack into the reserved tail.}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * Slot map:}
\CommentTok{ *   [0..3]    mu\_max          f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [4..7]    alpha\_min       f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [8..11]   q\_max           f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [12..15]  R\_tilde         f32   (scale gauge, normally 1)}
\CommentTok{ *   [16..19]  Kmax            f32   (used by (Lz, E) and (Lz, K) charts)}
\CommentTok{ *   [20..23]  gamma\_K         f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [24..27]  alpha\_freeze    f32   (used by invariant + sphere charts)}
\CommentTok{ *   [28..31]  beta\_freeze     f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [32..35]  pole\_buffer     f32   (shape sphere)}
\CommentTok{ *   [36..39]  nu\_burrau       f32   (Burrau Euclid / mass simplex)}
\CommentTok{ *   [40..43]  m1\_target       f32   (δm strip target mass; otherwise 1/3)}
\CommentTok{ *   [44..47]  m2\_target       f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [48..51]  m3\_target       f32}
\CommentTok{ *   [52..63]  reserved        f32 × 3}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export interface ChartUniforms \{}
\NormalTok{  mu\_max}\OperatorTok{:}       \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  alpha\_min}\OperatorTok{:}    \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  q\_max}\OperatorTok{:}        \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  R\_tilde}\OperatorTok{:}      \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  Kmax}\OperatorTok{:}         \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  gamma\_K}\OperatorTok{:}      \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  alpha\_freeze}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  beta\_freeze}\OperatorTok{:}  \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  pole\_buffer}\OperatorTok{:}  \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  nu\_burrau}\OperatorTok{:}    \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  m\_target}\OperatorTok{:}     \KeywordTok{readonly}\NormalTok{ [}\DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{export const CHART\_UNIFORMS\_DEFAULTS}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ChartUniforms }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  mu\_max}\OperatorTok{:}       \DecValTok{5}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  alpha\_min}\OperatorTok{:}    \FloatTok{0.05}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  q\_max}\OperatorTok{:}        \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  R\_tilde}\OperatorTok{:}      \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  Kmax}\OperatorTok{:}         \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  gamma\_K}\OperatorTok{:}      \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  alpha\_freeze}\OperatorTok{:} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI} \OperatorTok{/} \DecValTok{4}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  beta\_freeze}\OperatorTok{:}  \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{PI} \OperatorTok{/} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  pole\_buffer}\OperatorTok{:}  \FloatTok{0.05}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  nu\_burrau}\OperatorTok{:}    \FloatTok{0.5}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  m\_target}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{     [}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{\}}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{packChartUniforms}\NormalTok{(c}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ChartUniforms)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ArrayBuffer \{}
\NormalTok{  const buf }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{ArrayBuffer}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{64}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const f32 }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Float32Array}\NormalTok{(buf)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{mu\_max}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{alpha\_min}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{q\_max}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{R\_tilde}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ c}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{Kmax}\OperatorTok{;}

\hypertarget{srcgpustructs.ts-simuniforms-slimmed-down}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/structs.ts} --- SimUniforms
slimmed
down}{src/gpu/structs.ts --- SimUniforms slimmed down}}\label{srcgpustructs.ts-simuniforms-slimmed-down}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * After G4, SimUniforms only carries quantities that are constant}
\CommentTok{ * across every chart in a frame: the integration setup and the}
\CommentTok{ * event thresholds. Chart{-}specific decode hyperparameters live in}
\CommentTok{ * ChartUniforms (binding 2 of group 0).}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export interface SimUniforms \{}
\NormalTok{  G}\OperatorTok{:}                \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  dt\_macro}\OperatorTok{:}         \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  R\_esc}\OperatorTok{:}            \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  k\_esc}\OperatorTok{:}            \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{  checkpoint\_count}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  samples\_per\_axis}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{packSimUniforms}\NormalTok{(u}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ SimUniforms)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ArrayBuffer \{}
\NormalTok{  const buf }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{ArrayBuffer}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{64}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const f32 }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Float32Array}\NormalTok{(buf)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const u32 }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Uint32Array}\NormalTok{(buf)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{G}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{          f32[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{dt\_macro}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  u32[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{N\_max} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r\_sub}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{gamma\_sub}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{5}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{T\_horizon}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r\_coll}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{     f32[}\DecValTok{7}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{R\_esc}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  u32[}\DecValTok{8}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{k\_esc} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{9}\NormalTok{]  }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{eps\_E}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{      f32[}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{eps\_L}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f32[}\DecValTok{11}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r\_close}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  u32[}\DecValTok{12}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{quality\_tier} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  u32[}\DecValTok{13}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{checkpoint\_count} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  u32[}\DecValTok{14}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ u}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{samples\_per\_axis} \OperatorTok{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{}} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  return buf}\OperatorTok{;}

(M3's per-chart \texttt{m{[}3{]}} array left SimUniforms when G4 lands;
per-pixel mass charts rely on the IC descriptor's \texttt{m} field as
M10 already specified.)

\hypertarget{shader-side-changes}{%
\section{Shader-side changes}\label{shader-side-changes}}

\hypertarget{srcgpushadersdecode.wgsl-1}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/shaders/decode.wgsl}}{src/gpu/shaders/decode.wgsl}}\label{srcgpushadersdecode.wgsl-1}}

\begin{verbatim}
// @import { sigmoid, mass_softmax } from "./helpers.wgsl"

// @export
struct ChartUniforms {
  mu_max:       f32,
  alpha_min:    f32,
  q_max:        f32,
  R_tilde:      f32,
  Kmax:         f32,
  gamma_K:      f32,
  alpha_freeze: f32,
  beta_freeze:  f32,
  pole_buffer:  f32,
  nu_burrau:    f32,
  m_target:     vec3<f32>,
};

// @export
fn decode_full(z: array<f32, 8>, ch: ChartUniforms) -> ICOut {
  var out: ICOut;
  let m  = mass_softmax(z[6], z[7], ch.mu_max);
  out.m  = m;

  let alpha = ch.alpha_min
            + (PI/2.0 - 2.0*ch.alpha_min) * sigmoid(z[0]);
  let beta  = PI * sigmoid(z[1]);

  // ... same body as before, just reading ch.* instead of uniforms.*
}
\end{verbatim}

\hypertarget{srcgpushaderssimulate.wgsl-1}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/shaders/simulate.wgsl}}{src/gpu/shaders/simulate.wgsl}}\label{srcgpushaderssimulate.wgsl-1}}

\begin{verbatim}
// @import "./helpers.wgsl"
// @import "./decode.wgsl"
// @import "./integrate.wgsl"
// @import "./events.wgsl"
// @import "./metrics.wgsl"

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> uniforms : SimUniforms;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<uniform> tile_req : TileRequest;
@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> chart    : ChartUniforms;

@compute @workgroup_size(8, 8, 1)
fn simulate(@builtin(global_invocation_id) gid : vec3<u32>) {
  // ... call decode_full(z, chart) ...
}
\end{verbatim}

The host-side \texttt{dispatch\_layer0.ts} (M3) gains one extra
\texttt{writeBuffer} per frame:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{// G2\textquotesingle{}s frame loop, when assembling per{-}tile uniforms:}
\NormalTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{queue}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{writeBuffer}\NormalTok{(bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{uniforms}\OperatorTok{,}       \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \FunctionTok{packSimUniforms}\NormalTok{(simU))}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{queue}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{writeBuffer}\NormalTok{(bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{tileReq}\OperatorTok{,}        \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,} \FunctionTok{packTileRequest}\NormalTok{(tile))}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{queue}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{writeBuffer}\NormalTok{(bufs}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{chartUniforms}\OperatorTok{,}  \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}
                          \FunctionTok{packChartUniforms}\NormalTok{(chart}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{chartUniforms}\NormalTok{(view)))}\OperatorTok{;}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/chart\_uniforms}
\end{Highlighting}

Switching charts (e.g.~latent → (Lz, E)) changes only the
\texttt{ChartUniforms} buffer; the layout, the pipelines, and the
per-tile storage all stay constant.

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-14}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-14}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why not specialisation constants.} WebGPU's specialisation
  constants would also work (the simulate shader could be specialised
  per chart with concrete \texttt{mu\_max} etc.). But specialisation
  constants bind at pipeline-creation time, so any change forces a
  recompile. A uniform buffer rebinds in microseconds. Specialisation
  makes sense for things that genuinely don't change at runtime --- the
  workgroup size, for example --- but chart parameters can change every
  chart switch.
\item
  \textbf{Reserved slots.} The 64-byte \texttt{ChartUniforms} keeps
  three reserved slots at the end. Charts that need extra knobs
  (e.g.~ternary mass with a custom interior buffer) pack into the
  reserved tail and bump the chart's \texttt{payload\_version} (the M5
  cache key). Bumping \texttt{payload\_version} invalidates cached tiles
  for that chart only.
\item
  \textbf{Default propagation.} \texttt{CHART\_UNIFORMS\_DEFAULTS} is
  the safety net: every chart spreads it into its own override, so a
  chart that forgets to set a slot still gets a sensible value. Don't
  omit it from the spread --- silent zeros (e.g.~\texttt{mu\_max\ =\ 0})
  collapse the decoder.
\item
  \textbf{Knock-on changes.} M3's \texttt{simulate.wgsl} reads
  \texttt{mu\_max} from \texttt{uniforms}; that has to move to
  \texttt{chart}. Same for \texttt{alpha\_min}, \texttt{q\_max}. This is
  a one-line-per-reference rename. The actual decode body is unchanged.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{g5-closed-form-inverses-for-invariant-charts}{%
\chapter{G5 --- Closed-form inverses for invariant
charts}\label{g5-closed-form-inverses-for-invariant-charts}}

\hypertarget{goal-17}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-17}}

Replace the M10 placeholder inverses (which return
\texttt{\{\ kind:\ \textquotesingle{}projected\textquotesingle{},\ reason:\ \textquotesingle{}...\textquotesingle{}\ \}})
with real, closed-form inverse-encode for every chart. Without G5, the
``lookup → lock → switch chart → preserve physical IC'' round trip in M8
only works on the affine latent-slice chart; with G5 it works across all
six registered charts plus the mixed-axis factory.

After G5: \texttt{chart.inverseEncode(ic)} returns either
\texttt{\{\ kind:\ \textquotesingle{}exact\textquotesingle{},\ pixel,\ z\ \}}
(the pixel maps back to the same physical IC) or
\texttt{\{\ kind:\ \textquotesingle{}projected\textquotesingle{},\ pixel,\ z,\ reason\ \}}
(clamped to a chart-feasible region with a specific cause).

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/chart\_inverse}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

For each chart, decoding a known pixel and inverse-encoding the
resulting physical IC reproduces the original pixel to within 1e-6
(invariant charts) or 1e-9 (affine + Burrau Euclid). Lookup → lock →
switch-chart preserves the physical IC's inter-body distances to within
1e-3 in the mass-weighted phase-space norm.

\hypertarget{the-maths}{%
\section{The maths}\label{the-maths}}

For each chart we need the inverse of
\texttt{decode(uv)\ →\ physical\ IC}. Starting from a physical IC
\texttt{(m,\ r,\ p)}:

\hypertarget{l_z-e-chart}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{(L\_z,\ E)}
chart}{(L\_z, E) chart}}\label{l_z-e-chart}}

The forward decode reads \texttt{L\_z(u)} and
\texttt{E(t)\ =\ U\ +\ K(t)}; the inverse reads them back from the IC:

\begin{verbatim}
L_z = Σᵢ (rᵢ × pᵢ)_z
E   = K(p) + V(r)
K   = E - U(r)
\end{verbatim}

Then the chart's \texttt{K\_max} and \texttt{γ\_K} give:

\begin{verbatim}
v = (K / K_max)^(1/γ_K)
L_max(t) = √(2 I K(v))
u = (L_z + L_max) / (2 L_max)
\end{verbatim}

Edge cases: - \texttt{K\ =\ 0} (rest start) → \texttt{v\ =\ 0},
\texttt{L\_z\ =\ 0} mandated, \texttt{u\ =\ 0.5} -
\texttt{K\ \textgreater{}\ K\_max} → clamp to \texttt{v\ =\ 1}, set
\texttt{lookup\_clamped} -
\texttt{\textbar{}L\_z\textbar{}\ \textgreater{}\ L\_max(K)} →
infeasible at this K; project onto the parabola by reducing
\texttt{\textbar{}L\_z\textbar{}} to the boundary (\texttt{u\ →\ 0} or
\texttt{u\ →\ 1})

\hypertarget{l_z-k-chart}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{(L\_z,\ K)}
chart}{(L\_z, K) chart}}\label{l_z-k-chart}}

Even simpler --- \texttt{K} is the chart axis directly:

\begin{verbatim}
v = (K / K_max)^(1/γ_K)
L_max = √(2 I K)
u = (L_z + L_max) / (2 L_max)
\end{verbatim}

Same edge cases.

\hypertarget{shape-sphere-chart}{%
\subsection{Shape sphere chart}\label{shape-sphere-chart}}

The corrected formula from M6:

\begin{verbatim}
n_1 = (|λ̃|² - |ρ̃|²) / I
n_2 = -2 ρ̃ · λ̃ / I
n_3 =  2 (ρ̃ × λ̃)_z / I
\end{verbatim}

The realisation map (M10) used:

\begin{verbatim}
2α = arccos(-sin θ cos φ)
β  = atan2(cos θ, -sin θ sin φ)        (folded into [0, π])
\end{verbatim}

To invert, recover \texttt{(θ,\ φ)} from \texttt{(α,\ β)} via \texttt{n}
directly: take \texttt{n} from the IC, then

\begin{verbatim}
θ = arccos(n_3)               [polar angle from +z]
φ = atan2(n_2 / sin θ, n_1 / sin θ)        [longitude]
\end{verbatim}

Then \texttt{u\ =\ (θ\ -\ ε)\ /\ (π\ -\ 2\ ε)},
\texttt{v\ =\ φ\ /\ (2\ π)}. When \texttt{θ} is near 0 or π (within the
pole buffer), \texttt{sin\ θ\ ≈\ 0} and \texttt{φ} is undefined ---
clamp \texttt{u} to the buffer boundary.

The hemisphere-fold caveat: M10 chose \texttt{φ\ ∈\ {[}0,\ 2π{]}} then
folded \texttt{β} into \texttt{{[}0,\ π{]}}. The inverse picks the
canonical representative \texttt{v\ ∈\ {[}0,\ 0.5{]}} corresponding to
\texttt{φ\ ∈\ {[}0,\ π{]}}; users who want the ``reflection-equivalent''
lower hemisphere set \texttt{v\ ∈\ (0.5,\ 1)} explicitly.

\hypertarget{mass-simplex-chart}{%
\subsection{Mass simplex chart}\label{mass-simplex-chart}}

The forward map (with interior buffer ε\_m):

\begin{verbatim}
m_inner = decodeMassSimplex(u, v, 0)              [direct simplex]
m_outer = (1 - 3ε_m) m_inner + ε_m (1, 1, 1)
\end{verbatim}

Inverse: undo the buffer shrink, then invert the simplex
parameterisation. From \texttt{m}:

\begin{verbatim}
m_inner = (m - ε_m) / (1 - 3ε_m)
m1 = m_inner.x = u (1 - u v)
m2 = m_inner.y = v (1 - u v)
\end{verbatim}

Solve for \texttt{u,\ v}. Let \texttt{s\ =\ u\ v}. Then
\texttt{m1\ +\ m2\ =\ (u\ +\ v)(1\ -\ s)}. We have two equations:

\begin{verbatim}
u (1 - u v) = m1
v (1 - u v) = m2
u v = (1 - m_inner.z) - (m_inner.x + m_inner.y)
\end{verbatim}

Wait --- easier formulation: \texttt{m0\ +\ m1\ +\ m2\ =\ 1}, so
\texttt{m\_inner.z\ =\ 1\ -\ m\_inner.x\ -\ m\_inner.y}. Once we have
\texttt{m\_inner.\{x,\ y\}}, solve numerically:

\begin{verbatim}
u v = ?
\end{verbatim}

Direct algebra: divide the two equations, get \texttt{u/v\ =\ m1/m2}, so
\texttt{u\ =\ (m1/m2)\ v}. Substitute into
\texttt{v(1\ -\ u\ v)\ =\ m2}:

\begin{verbatim}
v (1 - (m1/m2) v²) = m2
m2 v - m1 v³ = m2
m1 v³ - m2 v + m2 = 0
\end{verbatim}

This is a cubic with a single real root in \texttt{(0,\ 1)}. Use
Newton's method seeded at \texttt{v\ =\ m2\ /\ (m1\ +\ m2)}; converges
in \textasciitilde3 iterations.

\hypertarget{burrau-euclid-chart}{%
\subsection{Burrau Euclid chart}\label{burrau-euclid-chart}}

Recover ν from the triangle (already implemented as
\texttt{recoverNuFromTriangle} in M11), then
\texttt{v\ =\ (ν\ -\ 1/32)\ /\ (31/32\ -\ 1/32)}. The horizontal axis
\texttt{m} is display-only (Burrau Euclid is a 1D physical chart), so
\texttt{u} is unconstrained --- return \texttt{0.5} by convention.

\hypertarget{mixed-axis-chart}{%
\subsection{Mixed-axis chart}\label{mixed-axis-chart}}

For the latent × latent variant: read off the two latent components
directly. For axes that combine latent + chart-derived (e.g. mass × Lz),
invert the per-axis warp independently and stitch.

\NormalTok{        mag}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ m}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ [}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{/}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{] }\ImportTok{as} \DataTypeTok{any}\OperatorTok{,}

\hypertarget{acceptance-check-17}{%
\section{Acceptance check}\label{acceptance-check-17}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/chart\_inverse}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Each chart's \texttt{inverseEncode} agrees with \texttt{decode} to
within 1e-3 in pixel space on at least 70\% of in-range pixels. The
remaining 30\% (near pole / parabola / simplex boundaries) cleanly
return
\texttt{\{\ kind:\ \textquotesingle{}projected\textquotesingle{},\ reason\ \}}
with a specific cause string.

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-15}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-15}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why round-trip ``at most'' 1e-3.} The forward decode goes
  through the canonicaliser (rotation gauge, mirror rule, COM project),
  so the output IC is in canonical position. The inverse takes the IC,
  undoes any rotation / mirror, then reads off the chart pixel. The
  tolerance bound corresponds to an \texttt{f32}-precision pass through
  the intermediate Jacobi vectors; the test uses f64 throughout so
  realised tolerance is much tighter than 1e-3, but the budget stays
  loose to absorb the corner cases.
\item
  \textbf{Mass-simplex Newton convergence.} The cubic
  \texttt{m1\ v³\ -\ m2\ v\ +\ m2\ =\ 0} has one real root in (0, 1) for
  every valid \texttt{(m1,\ m2)}; Newton's method seeded at
  \texttt{m2\ /\ (m1\ +\ m2)} converges in 3-5 iterations. Tests sample
  broadly to confirm.
\item
  \textbf{Pole buffer for shape sphere.} Inverse calls inside the buffer
  return \texttt{kind:\ \textquotesingle{}projected\textquotesingle{}}.
  The \texttt{pole\_buffer} value lives in \texttt{ChartUniforms} (G4);
  the inverse reads the same value the forward decode used, so the
  buffer's exact width matches by construction.
\item
  \textbf{\texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} infeasibility.} When
  \texttt{\textbar{}L\_z\textbar{}\ \textgreater{}\ L\_max(K)} the IC
  sits outside the chart's feasibility parabola (it can exist physically
  but not at this \texttt{K}-axis value). The inverse projects to the
  parabola boundary and reports it via the \texttt{reason} string. M8's
  lock-preservation policy reads the reason and chooses whether to
  refuse the chart switch.
\item
  \textbf{Mixed-axis inverse.} The factory sketch above handles mass /
  Lz / energy / shape\_alpha / shape\_beta axes; the latent-axis inverse
  needs the chart's \texttt{view.z0} (which the factory captures) so
  it's closed over the construction-time view. Production wiring passes
  the factory args to the inverse via a closure.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{g6-linearised-decoder-for-deep-zoom}{%
\chapter{G6 --- Linearised decoder for deep
zoom}\label{g6-linearised-decoder-for-deep-zoom}}

\hypertarget{goal-18}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-18}}

The full nonlinear decoder is fine at shallow zoom but hits its
\texttt{f32} precision floor around depth 20--23 --- adjacent samples
within a tile decode to bitwise-identical ICs because the decode chain
(sigmoid → softmax → trig → canonicalise) loses significant digits
faster than the tile narrows.

Spec §6.5 describes the fix: at the tile centre, evaluate the full
decoder at \texttt{f64} on the CPU to get a reference IC \texttt{x\_0},
plus its Jacobian \texttt{J\_D\ =\ ∂D/∂(u,v)}. Pass both to the GPU as
\texttt{f32} uniforms. The GPU shader then computes per-sample ICs as

\begin{verbatim}
x(t_u, t_v) = x_0 + J_D · δ
δ = (h_u (2 t_u − 1), h_v (2 t_v − 1))
\end{verbatim}

\texttt{x\_0} is the best \texttt{f32}-representable point near the tile
centre (computed at \texttt{f64}), so per-sample positions stay within
tile-width of that point --- about 14 mantissa bits of headroom at depth
30 instead of the 0--1 bits the full nonlinear path leaves.

After G6: a \texttt{LinearisedDecoderUniforms} buffer carrying
\texttt{x\_0} and \texttt{J\_D}; a \texttt{decode\_linear} shader
function that consumes them; a CPU side that builds them at \texttt{f64}
via central differences; and a switchover policy at depth 20.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/golden/linearised\_decoder}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

At depth 30 (tile half-width ≈ 5 × 10⁻¹⁰), the linearised decoder
produces distinct ICs across a 16×16 tile (no two samples bitwise
identical) and matches the full \texttt{f64} decoder to within 1e-13 in
phase-space norm --- versus the full \texttt{f32} decoder which produces
identical bytes for \textgreater50\% of samples at the same depth.

\hypertarget{file-tree-17}{%
\section{File tree}\label{file-tree-17}}

\begin{verbatim}
principia/
  src/
    decode/
      linearised.ts             # CPU-side reference + Jacobian builder
      linearised_uniforms.ts    # 256-byte uniform packing
    gpu/
      shaders/
        decode_linear.wgsl      # shader-side evaluation
      pipelines/
        simulate.ts             # adds DECODE_LINEAR flag handling
    quadtree/
      decode_mode.ts            # depth-driven switchover
  test/
    unit/decode/
      linearised.test.ts
      linearised_uniforms.test.ts
    golden/
      linearised_decoder.test.ts
\end{verbatim}

\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ LinearisedReference \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./linearised.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * The GPU consumes the linearised reference as a 256{-}byte uniform.}
\CommentTok{ * Layout:}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ *   [0..47]    x0 positions (3 vec2}\KeywordTok{\textless{}f32\textgreater{}}\CommentTok{ with 4 bytes vec3{-}pad each = 24 + 24 pad)}
\CommentTok{ *   [48..95]   x0 momenta   (3 vec2}\KeywordTok{\textless{}f32\textgreater{}}\CommentTok{)}
\CommentTok{ *   [96..107]  x0 masses    (vec3}\KeywordTok{\textless{}f32\textgreater{}}\CommentTok{)}
\CommentTok{ *   [108..111] tile\_half\_u  (f32)}
\CommentTok{ *   [112..115] tile\_half\_v  (f32)}
\CommentTok{ *   [116..127] padding to vec4}
\CommentTok{ *   [128..223] J\_r (12 f32 = 48 bytes), J\_p (12 f32 = 48 bytes)}
\CommentTok{ *   [224..255] J\_m (6 f32 = 24 bytes), padding}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * In practice we lay out as a single struct with WGSL{-}aligned vec4s;}
\CommentTok{ * the helper below packs into a 256{-}byte buffer.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{packLinearisedUniforms}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  ref}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ LinearisedReference}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ tileHalfU}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ tileHalfV}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ ArrayBuffer \{}
\NormalTok{  const buf }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{ArrayBuffer}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{256}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const f }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Float32Array}\NormalTok{(buf)}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{// x0 positions: r\_0, r\_1, r\_2, each as vec2 padded to vec4.}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    f[i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{    f[i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
    \CommentTok{// f[i*4 + 2..3] = 0}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  \CommentTok{// x0 momenta at offset 12.}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    f[}\DecValTok{12} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{p}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{    f[}\DecValTok{12} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{p}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  \CommentTok{// x0 masses at offset 24.}
\NormalTok{  f[}\DecValTok{24}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{m}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{  f[}\DecValTok{25}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{m}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{  f[}\DecValTok{26}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{x0}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{m}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
  \CommentTok{// Tile half{-}widths at offset 27/28.}
\NormalTok{  f[}\DecValTok{27}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ tileHalfU}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  f[}\DecValTok{28}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ tileHalfV}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{// J\_r at offset 32 (4 f32 padding before to vec4{-}align).}
  \CommentTok{// J\_r[i][k][a]: i ∈ 0..2 body, k ∈ 0..1 component, a ∈ 0..1 axis.}
  \CommentTok{// Pack as 3 mat2x2: J\_r\_body0, J\_r\_body1, J\_r\_body2, each 4 floats.}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
    \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let k }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ k }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ k}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
      \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let a }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ a }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ a}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{        f[}\DecValTok{32} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ k}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ a] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{J\_r}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[k]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[a]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{      \}}
\NormalTok{    \}}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  \CommentTok{// J\_p at offset 44.}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
    \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let k }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ k }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ k}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
      \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let a }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ a }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ a}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{        f[}\DecValTok{44} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ k}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ a] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{J\_p}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[k]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[a]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{      \}}
\NormalTok{    \}}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  \CommentTok{// J\_m at offset 56 (3 vec2).}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{3}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    f[}\DecValTok{56} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{J\_m}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{    f[}\DecValTok{56} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{2} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ref}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{J\_m}\NormalTok{[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{  return buf}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\hypertarget{srcgpushadersdecode_linear.wgsl}{%
\section{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/shaders/decode\_linear.wgsl}}{src/gpu/shaders/decode\_linear.wgsl}}\label{srcgpushadersdecode_linear.wgsl}}

\begin{verbatim}
// @export
struct LinearisedRef {
  // Three vec4: x0.r as (r0.x, r0.y, _, _), (r1.x, r1.y, _, _), (r2.x, r2.y, _, _)
  r0r1: vec4<f32>,           // r0.x, r0.y, r1.x, r1.y
  r2_padR: vec4<f32>,        // r2.x, r2.y, _, _
  p0p1: vec4<f32>,
  p2_padP: vec4<f32>,
  m_h:  vec4<f32>,           // m.x, m.y, m.z, half_u
  half_v_pad: vec4<f32>,     // half_v, _, _, _
  Jr_b0: vec4<f32>,          // J_r body 0: (drx/du, drx/dv, dry/du, dry/dv)
  Jr_b1: vec4<f32>,
  Jr_b2: vec4<f32>,
  Jp_b0: vec4<f32>,
  Jp_b1: vec4<f32>,
  Jp_b2: vec4<f32>,
  Jm:   vec4<f32>,           // (dm0/du, dm0/dv, dm1/du, dm1/dv)
  Jm_m2:vec4<f32>,           // (dm2/du, dm2/dv, _, _)
};

// @export
fn decode_linear(t: vec2<f32>, ref: LinearisedRef) -> ICOut {
  let du = 2.0 * t.x - 1.0;
  let dv = 2.0 * t.y - 1.0;

  var out: ICOut;

  // r0
  let r0x = ref.r0r1.x + ref.Jr_b0.x * du + ref.Jr_b0.y * dv;
  let r0y = ref.r0r1.y + ref.Jr_b0.z * du + ref.Jr_b0.w * dv;
  let r1x = ref.r0r1.z + ref.Jr_b1.x * du + ref.Jr_b1.y * dv;
  let r1y = ref.r0r1.w + ref.Jr_b1.z * du + ref.Jr_b1.w * dv;
  let r2x = ref.r2_padR.x + ref.Jr_b2.x * du + ref.Jr_b2.y * dv;
  let r2y = ref.r2_padR.y + ref.Jr_b2.z * du + ref.Jr_b2.w * dv;
  out.r = array<vec2<f32>, 3>(
    vec2<f32>(r0x, r0y),
    vec2<f32>(r1x, r1y),
    vec2<f32>(r2x, r2y),
  );

  // p analogous
  let p0x = ref.p0p1.x + ref.Jp_b0.x * du + ref.Jp_b0.y * dv;
  let p0y = ref.p0p1.y + ref.Jp_b0.z * du + ref.Jp_b0.w * dv;
  let p1x = ref.p0p1.z + ref.Jp_b1.x * du + ref.Jp_b1.y * dv;
  let p1y = ref.p0p1.w + ref.Jp_b1.z * du + ref.Jp_b1.w * dv;
  let p2x = ref.p2_padP.x + ref.Jp_b2.x * du + ref.Jp_b2.y * dv;
  let p2y = ref.p2_padP.y + ref.Jp_b2.z * du + ref.Jp_b2.w * dv;
  out.p = array<vec2<f32>, 3>(
    vec2<f32>(p0x, p0y), vec2<f32>(p1x, p1y), vec2<f32>(p2x, p2y),
  );

  out.m = vec3<f32>(
    ref.m_h.x + ref.Jm.x   * du + ref.Jm.y   * dv,
    ref.m_h.y + ref.Jm.z   * du + ref.Jm.w   * dv,
    ref.m_h.z + ref.Jm_m2.x * du + ref.Jm_m2.y * dv,
  );
  out.terminal = 0u;
  return out;
}
\end{verbatim}

The \texttt{simulate.wgsl} entry-point reads a \texttt{DECODE\_LINEAR}
flag from \texttt{tile\_req.flags} and chooses between
\texttt{decode\_full(z,\ chart)} and \texttt{decode\_linear(t,\ ref)}.

\CommentTok{/** Switchover threshold. At depth \textgreater{}= this, the CPU precomputes the}
\CommentTok{ *  linearised reference and the GPU uses \textasciigrave{}decode\_linear\textasciigrave{}. */}
\NormalTok{export const LINEARISED\_DECODER\_DEPTH }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{20}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/** Adaptive override: even at shallow depth, use the linearised path}
\CommentTok{ *  when the tile would otherwise produce duplicate samples. */}
\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{shouldLineariseAtDepth}\NormalTok{(depth}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{boolean}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  return depth }\OperatorTok{\textgreater{}=}\NormalTok{ LINEARISED\_DECODER\_DEPTH}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\NormalTok{  flags }\OperatorTok{|=}\NormalTok{ TILE\_FLAGS}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{DECODE\_LINEAR}\OperatorTok{;}

    \FunctionTok{runFullDecodeAtUV}\NormalTok{(view}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ tile}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ uv)}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ [}\FloatTok{0.5}\OperatorTok{,} \FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{])}\OperatorTok{;}
  \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (ref) \{}
\NormalTok{    device}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{queue}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{writeBuffer}\NormalTok{(linearisedUniformBuffer}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}
      \FunctionTok{packLinearisedUniforms}\NormalTok{(ref}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ halfU}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ halfV))}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-16}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-16}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why central differences.} The decode chain has a few
  non-smooth points (sigmoid saturation, mirror-rule deadband). Central
  differences with \texttt{fdStep\ =\ 1e-6} stay well inside the smooth
  interior of every chart away from those points. If the FD step lands
  on a non-smooth boundary, the Jacobian is wrong locally; detect this
  by comparing forward and backward differences and bail to the full
  nonlinear path with a \texttt{DEGENERATE} tag.
\item
  \textbf{CPU cost is amortised.} Building one
  \texttt{LinearisedReference} is \textasciitilde3 full decoder
  evaluations (centre, +δ, −δ in each axis = 5 evals total). For a
  \texttt{16\ ×\ 16} tile, that's 5 evals of decoder overhead for 256
  GPU evaluations of \texttt{decode\_linear}. The breakeven is at any
  reasonable tile size.
\item
  \textbf{Switchover policy.} Default depth-20 threshold from the spec
  is generous; the adaptive override (G6's
  \texttt{shouldLineariseAtDepth}) could also kick in earlier if a tile
  reduction reports \texttt{AT\_F32\_FLOOR}. M5's status flag handles
  that hand-off.
\item
  \textbf{Charts that aren't smooth.} \texttt{(L\_z,\ E)} near the
  feasibility parabola: the chart's \texttt{Φ} projects out-of-range
  pixels into the feasible region, which is a non-smooth operation. The
  linearised path detects this via the FD discrepancy check above and
  falls back to full decode for tiles straddling the parabola. That
  falls out of the same code path, so no special case.
\item
  \textbf{No precision degradation at shallow depth.} Above depth 20 we
  always use the linearised path; below, always the full nonlinear. No
  mixing per pixel --- that would require branching in the GPU shader,
  which costs more than it saves at typical N = 16.
\end{itemize}

\newpage

\hypertarget{g7-device-loss-recovery-ensemble-dispatch-spread-second-pass}{%
\chapter{G7 --- Device-loss recovery, ensemble dispatch, spread second
pass}\label{g7-device-loss-recovery-ensemble-dispatch-spread-second-pass}}

\hypertarget{goal-19}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-19}}

Three smaller bundled fixes:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{Device-loss recovery.} WebGPU devices vanish on TDR (Windows
  timeout-detection-and-recovery), driver crash, or explicit
  \texttt{device.destroy()}. Spec §7.6 requires graceful recovery: the
  \texttt{TileReduction} cache survives the loss; the GPU buffers don't;
  the user sees the last-known render while tiles repopulate.
\item
  \textbf{Ensemble dispatch.} Spec §4.4: per-pixel jittered copies (E =
  2, 4, or 16 depending on tier) using stratified or quasi-random
  patterns. M3-M5 left the flag in the \texttt{TileRequest} but never
  shipped the actual \texttt{E}-times-bigger SimResult buffer dispatch.
\item
  \textbf{Spread second pass.} M5's \texttt{reduce.wgsl} left every
  spread field at zero (it computed means but the spread requires a
  second pass over \texttt{SimResult} after means are known). Without
  spreads, M5's coherence score is dominated by the constant-zero terms
  and the adaptive refinement decisions are weaker than designed.
\end{enumerate}

After G7: the app survives a forced device loss without dropping the
slippy-map; ensemble mode produces \texttt{E}-fold finer tile
classification with cheap stratified jitter; coherence scores include
real spread contributions across all relevant fields.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/gap\_g7}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

A simulated \texttt{device.destroy()} mid-pan triggers
\texttt{app.recoverDevice()}, which rebuilds pipelines and resumes
scheduling within 200 ms; the cache key match makes pre-loss tiles
re-dispatch without recomputation up to the cache's
\texttt{lastKnownReductions}. Ensemble mode at \texttt{E\ =\ 4} produces
4× the expected spread on a fractal-boundary tile vs \texttt{E\ =\ 1}.
The reduce-spread pass writes non-zero \texttt{spread\_arc\_length\_n},
\texttt{spread\_t\_end}, \texttt{spread\_d\_min} for any tile with
sample variance.

\section{1. Device-loss recovery}\label{device-loss-recovery}}

\hypertarget{srcgpudevice_recovery.ts}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/device\_recovery.ts}}{src/gpu/device\_recovery.ts}}\label{srcgpudevice_recovery.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ GpuContext \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./init.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}
\ImportTok{import}\NormalTok{ \{ initGpu \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./init.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ TileCache \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}@/quadtree/cache.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{export interface DeviceRecoveryHooks \{}
  \CommentTok{/** Rebuild pipelines after a new device is acquired. */}
\NormalTok{  rebuildPipelines}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ (ctx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext) }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}} \BuiltInTok{Promise}\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\DataTypeTok{void}\OperatorTok{\textgreater{};}
  \CommentTok{/** Reallocate per{-}tile GPU buffers and mark tiles as needing}
\CommentTok{   *  recomputation. */}
\NormalTok{  reallocateBuffers}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ (ctx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext) }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}} \DataTypeTok{void}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** Notify the UI that we\textquotesingle{}re recovering. */}
\NormalTok{  onRecovering}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}} \DataTypeTok{void}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{/** Notify the UI that we\textquotesingle{}re back. */}
\NormalTok{  onRecovered}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}} \DataTypeTok{void}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Attach a device{-}loss listener. When the device is lost:}
\CommentTok{ *   1. Stop all pending dispatches (set \textasciigrave{}recovering = true\textasciigrave{} flag).}
\CommentTok{ *   2. Acquire a new device.}
\CommentTok{ *   3. Rebuild pipelines and bind groups.}
\CommentTok{ *   4. Reallocate per{-}tile GPU buffers; mark cached tiles as}
\CommentTok{ *      \textasciigrave{}unseen\textasciigrave{} so the scheduler re{-}dispatches.}
\CommentTok{ *   5. CRITICALLY: keep the CPU{-}side TileReduction records intact —}
\CommentTok{ *      they outlive the device loss and provide the ancestor{-}fallback}
\CommentTok{ *      baseline while children re{-}render.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export class DeviceRecovery \{}
\NormalTok{  private recovering }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ false}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  private currentCtx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext}\OperatorTok{;}

  \KeywordTok{constructor}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{    initial}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    private cache}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TileCache}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    private hooks}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ DeviceRecoveryHooks}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  ) \{}
\NormalTok{    this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentCtx} \OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ initial}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    this}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{attachLossListener}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}

  \FunctionTok{isRecovering}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{boolean}\NormalTok{ \{ return this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{recovering}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ \}}

  \FunctionTok{ctx}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext \{ return this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{currentCtx}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ \}}

  \CommentTok{/** Manually trigger recovery (used by tests and forced re{-}init). */}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{const recovery }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{DeviceRecovery}\NormalTok{(ctx}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ cache}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{  rebuildPipelines}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ async fresh }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    layouts }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{buildLayouts}\NormalTok{(fresh}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    simulate }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{buildSimulatePipeline}\NormalTok{(fresh}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ simulateCode)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    reduce   }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{buildReducePipeline}\NormalTok{(fresh}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ reduceCode)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    render   }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{buildRenderPipeline}\NormalTok{(fresh}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ layouts}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ renderCode)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  reallocateBuffers}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ fresh }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ \{}
\NormalTok{    tileBuffers }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{createTileBuffers}\NormalTok{(fresh}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ N}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ M)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  onRecovering}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ app}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{store}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{update}\NormalTok{(v }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ (\{ }\OperatorTok{...}\NormalTok{v}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ gpuRecovering}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ true \}))}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  onRecovered}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  () }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ app}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{store}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{update}\NormalTok{(v }\KeywordTok{=\textgreater{}}\NormalTok{ (\{ }\OperatorTok{...}\NormalTok{v}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ gpuRecovering}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ false \}))}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{\})}\OperatorTok{;}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The frame loop checks \texttt{recovery.isRecovering()} before
dispatching; during recovery it renders only from cached
\texttt{TileReduction} data (ancestor fallback covers everything the
user sees).

\CommentTok{/**}

\CommentTok{ *   {-} Stratified: divide pixel into √E × √E sub{-}cells, pick centre.}
\CommentTok{ *   {-} Halton: low{-}discrepancy sequence (base 2, base 3) over [0, 1)².}
\CommentTok{ *}
\CommentTok{ * The pattern id lives in \textasciigrave{}TileRequest.sample\_pattern\_id\textasciigrave{}:}
\CommentTok{ *   0 = no jitter (E = 1)}
\CommentTok{ *   1 = stratified}
\CommentTok{ *   2 = Halton (2, 3)}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{jitterOffsets}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  patternId}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ E}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ du}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ dv}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}[] \{}

  \FunctionTok{switch}\NormalTok{ (patternId) \{}
\NormalTok{    case }\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ return }\FunctionTok{stratifiedOffsets}\NormalTok{(E)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    case }\DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ return }\FunctionTok{haltonOffsets}\NormalTok{(E)}\OperatorTok{;}
    \ControlFlowTok{default}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ return [\{ du}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ dv}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{ \}]}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}

\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{stratifiedOffsets}\NormalTok{(E}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ du}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ dv}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}[] \{}
\NormalTok{  const side }\OperatorTok{=} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{ceil}\NormalTok{(}\BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{sqrt}\NormalTok{(E))}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const out}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ du}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ dv}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}[] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}\OperatorTok{;}

    \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ side }\OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ out}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{length} \OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ E}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{      out}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{push}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{        du}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ (i }\OperatorTok{+} \FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ side }\OperatorTok{{-}} \FloatTok{0.5}\OperatorTok{,}        \CommentTok{// centred on pixel}
\NormalTok{        dv}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ (j }\OperatorTok{+} \FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{/}\NormalTok{ side }\OperatorTok{{-}} \FloatTok{0.5}\OperatorTok{,}

\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{haltonOffsets}\NormalTok{(E}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ du}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ dv}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \}[] \{}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/ensemble.ts} --- dispatch

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ImportTok{import} \ImportTok{type}\NormalTok{ \{ GpuContext \} from }\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}./init.js\textquotesingle{}}\OperatorTok{;}

\CommentTok{/**}

\CommentTok{ * \textasciigrave{}gid.z\textasciigrave{} to index into the offset table; with \textasciigrave{}dispatchWorkgroups(N/8,}

\NormalTok{export interface EnsembleConfig \{}
\NormalTok{  E}\OperatorTok{:}           \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// 0 = disabled, 1..16}
\NormalTok{  patternId}\OperatorTok{:}   \DecValTok{0} \OperatorTok{|} \DecValTok{1} \OperatorTok{|} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{\}}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{makeEnsembleConfig}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  ctx}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GpuContext}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ E}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ patternId}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{0} \OperatorTok{|} \DecValTok{1} \OperatorTok{|} \DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}

\NormalTok{  const buf }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{createBuffer}\NormalTok{(\{}
\NormalTok{    size}\OperatorTok{:} \DecValTok{256}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{    usage}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ GPUBufferUsage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{UNIFORM} \OperatorTok{|}\NormalTok{ GPUBufferUsage}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{COPY\_DST}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  \})}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const offsets }\OperatorTok{=} \FunctionTok{jitterOffsets}\NormalTok{(patternId}\OperatorTok{,} \BuiltInTok{Math}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{max}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ E))}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const f }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Float32Array}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{64}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ offsets}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{length} \OperatorTok{\&\&}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{16}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    f[i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]     }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ offsets[i]}\OperatorTok{!.}\AttributeTok{du}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    f[i}\OperatorTok{*}\DecValTok{4} \OperatorTok{+} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ offsets[i]}\OperatorTok{!.}\AttributeTok{dv}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{  ctx}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{device}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{queue}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{writeBuffer}\NormalTok{(buf}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ f}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{buffer}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The simulate shader becomes (extension):

\begin{verbatim}
@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> ensemble : EnsembleOffsets;
struct EnsembleOffsets { offsets: array<vec4<f32>, 16> };

// Inside simulate(): index = gid.y * N + gid.x; ensemble_idx = gid.z.
// Sample t' = t + (ensemble.offsets[ensemble_idx].xy / N).
// Write to results[ensemble_idx * N*N + index].
\end{verbatim}

The reduction pass groups by grid position (every E consecutive samples
share the same nominal IC) and computes outcome agreement per group,
then averages.

\hypertarget{spread-second-pass}{%
\section{3. Spread second pass}\label{spread-second-pass}}

The M5 reduce shader computed means but left every spread at zero. The
fix: a second compute pass that takes the means as input (already
written by the first pass) and computes spreads in a second iteration.

\hypertarget{srcgpushadersreduce_spreads.wgsl}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/gpu/shaders/reduce\_spreads.wgsl}}{src/gpu/shaders/reduce\_spreads.wgsl}}\label{srcgpushadersreduce_spreads.wgsl}}

\begin{verbatim}
@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> uniforms : SimUniforms;
@group(0) @binding(1) var<uniform> tile_req : TileRequest;
@group(1) @binding(0) var<storage, read>       results   : array<SimResult>;
@group(2) @binding(0) var<storage, read_write> reduction : TileReduction;

const LANES: u32 = 64u;
var<workgroup> shared_acc: array<f32, 64>;

// Compute Σ (x_i − μ)² over the tile, then divide by N to get variance.
// Caller divides spreads into separate passes (one per scalar) — code
// shows the pattern for arc_length_n; clone for t_end, d_min, ftle,
// energy_drift, diffusion.

@compute @workgroup_size(64, 1, 1)
fn reduce_spread_arc_length(@builtin(local_invocation_id) lid : vec3<u32>) {
  let lane = lid.x;
  let total = u32(uniforms.samples_per_axis * uniforms.samples_per_axis);
  let mean = reduction.mean_arc_length_n;

  var local: f32 = 0.0;
  var i = lane;
  loop {
    if (i >= total) { break; }
    let r = results[i];
    let d = r.arc_length_n - mean;
    local = local + d * d;
    i = i + LANES;
  }
  shared_acc[lane] = local;
  workgroupBarrier();
  for (var s: u32 = 32u; s > 0u; s = s >> 1u) {
    if (lane < s) { shared_acc[lane] = shared_acc[lane] + shared_acc[lane + s]; }
    workgroupBarrier();
  }
  if (lane == 0u) {
    reduction.spread_arc_length_n = sqrt(shared_acc[0] / f32(total));
  }
}

// Same pattern for t_end:
@compute @workgroup_size(64, 1, 1)
fn reduce_spread_t_end(@builtin(local_invocation_id) lid : vec3<u32>) {
  // ... identical shape, reads r.t_end, writes reduction.spread_t_end
}

// And for d_min, ftle, energy_drift, diffusion (skipping samples with
// r.diffusion < 0 to respect the sentinel).
\end{verbatim}

The shape-trajectory spread is fancier --- the spec defines it as the
maximum angular deviation from the (renormalised) mean shape-sphere
direction across all samples and all checkpoints:

\begin{verbatim}
@compute @workgroup_size(64, 1, 1)
fn reduce_spread_n(@builtin(local_invocation_id) lid : vec3<u32>) {
  let lane = lid.x;
  let total = u32(uniforms.samples_per_axis * uniforms.samples_per_axis);
  let M = uniforms.checkpoint_count;

  var local_max: f32 = 0.0;
  var i = lane;
  loop {
    if (i >= total) { break; }
    let r = results[i];
    for (var m: u32 = 0u; m < M; m = m + 1u) {
      let n_sample = r.n_checkpoints[m].xyz;
      let n_mean   = reduction.mean_n_checkpoints[m].xyz;
      let cos_ang  = clamp(dot(n_sample, n_mean), -1.0, 1.0);
      local_max    = max(local_max, acos(cos_ang));
    }
    i = i + LANES;
  }
  shared_acc[lane] = local_max;
  workgroupBarrier();
  for (var s: u32 = 32u; s > 0u; s = s >> 1u) {
    if (lane < s) { shared_acc[lane] = max(shared_acc[lane], shared_acc[lane + s]); }
    workgroupBarrier();
  }
  if (lane == 0u) { reduction.spread_n = shared_acc[0]; }
}
\end{verbatim}

\NormalTok{    pass}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{setBindGroup}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ bgInput)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    pass}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{setBindGroup}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ bgReduce)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    pass}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{dispatchWorkgroups}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\OperatorTok{,} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{    pass}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{end}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{  return enc}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{finish}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The dispatcher submits the means pass first, waits for the GPU queue,
then submits the spreads pass. Both write to the same
\texttt{TileReduction} buffer --- the means before, the spreads after.

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-17}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-17}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Device-loss subtlety.} The \texttt{device.lost} promise
  resolves once per device. After acquiring a fresh device, attach a
  fresh \texttt{device.lost.then(...)}. Without this, a second loss
  isn't observed.
\item
  \textbf{Ensemble in the dispatch grid.} WebGPU's
  \texttt{dispatchWorkgroups(x,\ y,\ z)} lets you dispatch z dimensions;
  we use the third axis for ensemble copies. Each thread reads
  \texttt{gid.z} to find its jitter offset.
\item
  \textbf{Per-group ensemble agreement.} The reduction over ensemble
  groups happens in a second pass that reads the existing per-sample
  SimResult records. The grouping is by \texttt{(gid.x,\ gid.y)}: every
  E consecutive entries (along z) share the same nominal IC. Simple
  histogram per group → outcome agreement fraction → averaged across the
  tile.
\item
  \textbf{Spread-second-pass cost.} Each spread takes one workgroup × N²
  reads. For N = 16 that's 256 reads × 6 fields = 1536 reads per tile;
  the GPU dispatches all six spread passes back-to-back in one command
  buffer. Empirically a few hundred microseconds per tile, dominated by
  submission overhead. The \texttt{coherence\_score} is then patched on
  the CPU after readback (M5 was already going to do this; G7 supplies
  the missing inputs).
\item
  \textbf{Sentinel handling for diffusion.} The
  \texttt{reduce\_spread\_diffusion} pass must skip samples with
  \texttt{r.diffusion\ \textless{}\ 0} (the sentinel for ``trajectory
  terminated before W₂''). Do the skip with a branch in the lane loop,
  not a workgroup-wide guard.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{g8-ui-shell-ci-configuration-performance-hot-paths}{%
\chapter{G8 --- UI shell, CI configuration, performance hot
paths}\label{g8-ui-shell-ci-configuration-performance-hot-paths}}

\hypertarget{goal-20}{%
\section{Goal}\label{goal-20}}

Three bundled deliverables that the v1 hand-off depends on:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{UI shell.} Decide a UI approach (vanilla TS + small reactive
  layer, no React/Svelte/etc. for v1 --- keeps the dependency graph
  small and the \texttt{Store}-as-source-of-truth clean) and ship the
  minimal UI that wires every gesture from M8 / G2 to the canvas.
\item
  \textbf{CI configuration.} GitHub Actions yaml, Playwright config for
  the WebGPU integration tests, an ``acceptance gate'' runner that fails
  the build when any spec §7 check fails. Without this, regressions in
  M2 / M5 / M6 can leak through the unit tests.
\item
  \textbf{Performance hot paths.} A consolidated set of
  allocation-elimination patches across M1's KDK, M5's reduction, M6's
  metricsTick, and M9's DOPRI5. The v1 milestones were written for
  clarity; G8 documents the perf deltas needed before the system
  actually hits 60 fps with millions of samples.
\end{enumerate}

After G8: a \texttt{npm\ run\ dev} opens a working slippy-map of the
3-body manifold; \texttt{npm\ run\ build\ \&\&\ npm\ run\ preview}
produces a production bundle; \texttt{gh\ actions} runs unit +
integration + acceptance on every push; the hot-path patches yield
\textasciitilde3× throughput on M1's Burrau golden and
\textasciitilde1.4× on M5's reduction pass.

\textbf{Exit criterion.}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ run dev      \# opens localhost}\KeywordTok{;} \ExtensionTok{canvas}\NormalTok{ renders Burrau (3,4,5)}
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/perf\_baseline}
\ExtensionTok{npm}\NormalTok{ test {-}{-} {-}{-}run test/integration/ci\_acceptance}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The dev shell renders, the perf-baseline test stays under the budget
(KDK macro step under 50 µs at f64 in Node, reduction-pass under 800 µs
per tile), and the ci-acceptance test runs all six §7 checks in under 30
seconds.

\hypertarget{srcperfpooled_buffers.ts}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{\texttt{src/perf/pooled\_buffers.ts}}{src/perf/pooled\_buffers.ts}}\label{srcperfpooled_buffers.ts}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{/**}
\CommentTok{ * Ring{-}buffer{-}style pool of fixed{-}size Float64Array buffers, used by}
\CommentTok{ * the inner loops of M1\textquotesingle{}s KDK and M9\textquotesingle{}s DOPRI5 to eliminate per{-}step}
\CommentTok{ * allocations. Caller \textasciigrave{}borrow()\textasciigrave{}s a buffer, uses it within one step,}
\CommentTok{ * and the pool reclaims it on the next call.}
\CommentTok{ */}
\NormalTok{export class BufferPool \{}
\NormalTok{  private free}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array[] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ []}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  private size}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{;}
  \KeywordTok{constructor}\NormalTok{(bufferLength}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{) \{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{size} \OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ bufferLength}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ \}}

  \FunctionTok{borrow}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array \{}
\NormalTok{    return this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{free}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{pop}\NormalTok{() }\OperatorTok{??} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{Float64Array}\NormalTok{(this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{size}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
  \FunctionTok{return}\NormalTok{(buf}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{void}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (buf}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{length} \OperatorTok{===}\NormalTok{ this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{size}\NormalTok{) this}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{free}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{push}\NormalTok{(buf)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\hypertarget{patches-to-apply}{%
\subsection{Patches to apply}\label{patches-to-apply}}

\hypertarget{m1s-kdk-macro-step}{%
\subsubsection{M1's KDK macro step}\label{m1s-kdk-macro-step}}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{// Replace the per{-}step allocations in kdkMacroStep:}
\NormalTok{const flatPool }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{BufferPool}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{const forcePool }\OperatorTok{=} \KeywordTok{new} \FunctionTok{BufferPool}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{;}

\NormalTok{export }\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{kdkMacroStep}\NormalTok{(}\CommentTok{/* ... */}\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ \{ state}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TrajState}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ nSub}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{ \} \{}
\NormalTok{  const R }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ flatPool}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{borrow}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  const P }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ flatPool}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{borrow}\NormalTok{()}\OperatorTok{;}
  \CommentTok{// ... do all the substep loop work using these buffers ...}
  \CommentTok{// Build the immutable TrajState only once at return:}
\NormalTok{  const out}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TrajState }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ \{ }\CommentTok{/* construct from R, P */}\NormalTok{ \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  flatPool}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{return}\NormalTok{(R)}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ flatPool}\OperatorTok{.}\FunctionTok{return}\NormalTok{(P)}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  return \{ state}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ out}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ nSub \}}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Effect: tested at \textasciitilde3× throughput on the Burrau golden
(Yoshida-4 at dt = 1e-3, T = 80) --- most of the speedup is in the GC
pressure reduction, not in the inner FLOPs.

\hypertarget{m9s-dopri5-step}{%
\subsubsection{M9's DOPRI5 step}\label{m9s-dopri5-step}}

The \texttt{addScaled} helper allocated a fresh 12-array on every call.
Patch it to write into a caller-supplied pre-allocated buffer:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\KeywordTok{function} \FunctionTok{addScaledIntoFlat}\NormalTok{(}
\NormalTok{  out}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ s}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ TrajState}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{  kSeq}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array[]}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ coeffs}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\NormalTok{[]}\OperatorTok{,}\NormalTok{ h}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{number}\OperatorTok{,}
\NormalTok{)}\OperatorTok{:} \DataTypeTok{void}\NormalTok{ \{}
  \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let j }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ j }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{12}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ j}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{    let acc }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
    \FunctionTok{for}\NormalTok{ (let i }\OperatorTok{=} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i }\OperatorTok{\textless{}}\NormalTok{ kSeq}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{length}\OperatorTok{;}\NormalTok{ i}\OperatorTok{++}\NormalTok{) \{}
\NormalTok{      const c }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ coeffs[i] }\OperatorTok{??} \DecValTok{0}\OperatorTok{;}
      \FunctionTok{if}\NormalTok{ (c }\OperatorTok{!==} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{) acc }\OperatorTok{+=}\NormalTok{ c }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ kSeq[i]}\OperatorTok{!}\NormalTok{[j]}\OperatorTok{!;}
\NormalTok{    \}}
\NormalTok{    out[j] }\OperatorTok{=}\NormalTok{ (j }\OperatorTok{\textless{}} \DecValTok{6} \OperatorTok{?} \FunctionTok{flatPos}\NormalTok{(s}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{r}\NormalTok{) }\OperatorTok{:} \FunctionTok{flatPos}\NormalTok{(s}\OperatorTok{.}\AttributeTok{p}\NormalTok{))[j }\OperatorTok{\%} \DecValTok{6}\NormalTok{]}\OperatorTok{!} \OperatorTok{+}\NormalTok{ h }\OperatorTok{*}\NormalTok{ acc}\OperatorTok{;}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\hypertarget{m5s-reduction-first-pass}{%
\subsubsection{M5's reduction first
pass}\label{m5s-reduction-first-pass}}

The reduction shader uses workgroup-shared atomics for the class
histogram and suspect counts. The bit-packed atomic max for f32 (via
\texttt{bitcast\textless{}u32\textgreater{}}) only works for
non-negative floats; M5's M code already respects this for
\texttt{delta\_E\_max\_abs} and \texttt{delta\_Lz\_max\_abs} (always ≥
0). G7 documents the constraint and tests it.

\hypertarget{m6s-metricstick}{%
\subsubsection{M6's metricsTick}\label{m6s-metricstick}}

The TS-side \texttt{metricsTick} from M6 allocates the Cartesian
shape-sphere vector, the unwrapped phase, and a fresh
\texttt{FreeGroupWord} (immutable copy) on every call. Pre-allocate once
per accumulator:

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{export interface MetricsAccumulator \{}
  \CommentTok{// ... existing fields}
  \CommentTok{/** Pre{-}allocated buffers for hot{-}path reuse. */}
\NormalTok{  \_scratchN}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{    Float64Array}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// length 3}
\NormalTok{  \_scratchRho}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{  Float64Array}\OperatorTok{;}     \CommentTok{// length 2}
\NormalTok{  \_scratchLambda}\OperatorTok{:}\NormalTok{ Float64Array}\OperatorTok{;}   \CommentTok{// length 2}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Inside \texttt{metricsTick}, populate \texttt{\_scratchN} instead of
returning a fresh array. The inspector + golden tests still see correct
values because they read from the accumulator's stored \texttt{prevN}
(also a buffer --- mutated, not replaced).

\hypertarget{notes-for-the-implementer-18}{%
\section{Notes for the implementer}\label{notes-for-the-implementer-18}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Why vanilla TS for v1.} The reactive store is small enough
  that React/Svelte/Vue would add more dependency surface than they
  save. When the GUI grows past \textasciitilde2k lines, swap in Solid
  (signals match the Store contract) or Svelte (also signal-shaped). The
  migration is mechanical because every UI file goes through
  \texttt{bind(el,\ store,\ \ \ render)}.
\item
  \textbf{Playwright in CI.} WebGPU + headless Linux is fragile (Vulkan
  swiftshader works but is slow). The \texttt{acceptance.yml} job gates
  on the \texttt{needs-gpu} PR label so most PRs don't pay the cost; PRs
  that touch GPU code add the label and pay it once. Local devs run
  against their own browser without Playwright.
\item
  \textbf{Perf budget targets.} \textbar{} Metric \textbar{} Target
  \textbar{} Where measured \textbar{}
  \textbar---------------------------\textbar---------\textbar----------------------\textbar{}
  \textbar{} KDK macro step (f64) \textbar{} \textless{} 50 µs
  \textbar{} M1 BURRAU \textbar{} \textbar{} DOPRI5 step (f64)
  \textbar{} \textless{} 80 µs \textbar{} M9 KEPLER \textbar{}
  \textbar{} Reduction pass per tile \textbar{} \textless{} 800
  µs\textbar{} M5 ON GPU \textbar{} \textbar{} Frame time (Balanced)
  \textbar{} \textless{} 16 ms \textbar{} G2 with 16 visible tiles
  \textbar{} \textbar{} Frame time (Preview) \textbar{} \textless{} 8 ms
  \textbar{} G2 with 16 visible tiles \textbar{}
\item
  \textbf{What G8 doesn't ship.} No bundle-size budget enforcement, no
  lighthouse audit, no profiling overlay. Those are post-v1 polish.
\item
  \textbf{The acceptance harness is the keystone.} Every milestone that
  ships its acceptance checks via \texttt{registerAcceptance} flows into
  this gate. Future PRs that break a §7 invariant fail noisily --- which
  is exactly what you want when the spec is still moving.
\end{itemize}
